VS-Flash exposes flash as a large-capacity memory-semantic space and dynamically selects the execution engine according to runtime query and workload characteristics. It offloads throughput-oriented large-batch queries to a Computational Memory-Semantic Flash (CMS-Flash) device, while executing latency-sensitive small-batch queries on the host CPU. Both paths access the same resident segments, avoiding a separate host-DRAM replica. Across three billion-scale datasets, VS-Flash improves bulk-search throughput over vanilla Milvus by 36.8X on average, with up to a 57.4X improvement. Under mixed workloads, VS-Flash reduces the p99 latency of latency-sensitive requests by up to 24.8X while sustaining device-side bulk search. These results show that VS-Flash delivers scalable vector search beyond host DRAM capacity while jointly improving bulk throughput and small-request tail latency.

title: Do LLMs Really Lack Difference Awareness? Uncovering Heuristic Substitution in Group-Differentiating Fairness
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the issue of difference awareness in LLMs, defined as a model's ability to recognize and acknowledge meaningful differences between social groups in fairness decision-making. Previous studies have consistently shown that models perform poorly on such tasks, a finding commonly attributed to a lack of difference awareness. We propose an alternative account, which we term Fairness Heuristic Substitution: difference awareness is not necessarily absent, but the complex demand of simultaneously identifying relevant group differences and determining their implications for fairness decisions may lead models to substitute the simpler, more accessible equal-treatment heuristic, i.e., formal equality. Based on this hypothesis, we introduce TDD, a Two-stage Distinguish-Decide framework that explicitly decomposes fairness reasoning into first distinguishing contextually relevant group differences and then making the corresponding decision, thereby discouraging reliance on formal-equality shortcuts. (i) Across four benchmarks and ten models ranging from billions to trillions of parameters, TDD significantly outperforms one-stage baselines, even one strengthened through simulated test-set leakage. (ii) Combining TDD with neuron-level contrastive probing provides mechanistic evidence consistent with the Fairness Heuristic Substitution hypothesis by revealing two signatures of the formal-equality: a compact, locally coordinated representational structure and a pronounced activation bias under default reasoning. (iii) TDD's stage-wise decomposition uncovers overlooked failure modes in fairness reasoning, including heuristic displacement and misaligned stage dynamics.

title: DexGraspFlow: Topology-Aware SE(3) Flow Matching for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasp Generation
abstract: Differences in hand geometry, joint parameterization, and kinematic topology pose challenges for cross-embodiment dexterous grasp generation. However, spatial relations among links alone are insufficient to fully capture the hand's kinematic topology. We propose DexGraspFlow, a conditional link-level $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ flow-matching framework integrating geometric relations and kinematic topology. The framework encodes local object geometry, link geometry, and current poses. A dual-stream DiT models link--link coordination and link--object interaction, while attention biases derived from kinematic-tree distances provide explicit structural information for modeling evolving geometric interactions. The model jointly learns translational and rotational velocity fields, integrates them to generate link poses, and recovers joint configurations through inverse kinematics. Additionally, inference-time palm-orientation guidance enables controllable grasp generation without retraining. Across three robotic hands and 30 object--hand pairs, DexGraspFlow achieves a 95.33\% average simulation success rate, with an average generation latency, including inverse kinematics, approximately 49\% lower than that of a state-of-the-art baseline. Further experiments demonstrate zero-shot adaptability to seven finger-removal variants and palm-orientation control. A model trained on demonstrations for the deployed hand achieves a 91\% success rate over 100 real-robot grasping trials, supporting the framework's applicability to physical grasp execution.

title: FoundPDE: A generative foundation model for data-driven symbolic discovery of partial differential equations
abstract: Discovering governing partial differential equations (PDEs) from observed data is a central inverse problem in computational science and engineering: the goal is not only to predict trajectories, but to identify interpretable symbolic laws that can be analyzed and reused. Existing PDE discovery methods often depend on hand-designed libraries, accurate numerical derivatives, or per-equation symbolic search, making them fragile under sparse observations, noisy data, broad equation families, and unseen symbolic compositions. Here, we introduce FoundPDE, a pretrained data-to-symbol foundation model for PDE discovery. FoundPDE maps discretized spatio-temporal trajectories to symbolic equations with a transformer, uses Fourier and first-order spatial-derivative augmentation to expose complementary trajectory information, refines numerical coefficients, and supports downstream extension with improved generalization through few-shot fine-tuning and hierarchical discovery. On a clean in-domain benchmark spanning 20 PDE families, our model reaches 97.50% type recognition. Under coefficient shifts beyond the training support, type recognition remains 90.53%; under multiplicative Gaussian noise on the model input, it is 94.43% at a 2% noise level but falls to 52.09% at 10%. For unseen composite equations, few-shot fine-tuning reaches over 90% exact recovery on four held-out families, and we further develop a hierarchical discovery algorithm that recovers two-term composites without fine-tuning FoundPDE. By amortizing symbolic discovery across equation families, FoundPDE shifts PDE discovery from per-dataset search toward a reusable pretrained model that extends to new physics with limited additional data, a step toward foundation models that uncover interpretable governing laws directly from scientific data.

title: When Planning Problems Become Hard for LLMs: Separating Structural Complexity from Semantic Interpretability
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) struggle with classical planning, but benchmarks rarely distinguish structural difficulty from the difficulty of interpreting symbolic vocabulary. We examine seven STRIPS domains with BFS-optimal plan lengths. For predicting structural difficulty without solving an instance, the zero-training delete-relaxation heuristic $h_{\mathrm{add}}$ outperforms learned alternatives on held-out domains (mean Spearman $|ρ|=0.931$), including ridge regression ($0.707$), object count ($0.657$), and the episodic retrieval architecture ARC ($0.400$). ARC also fails to outperform a linear model using the same features. To isolate semantic effects, we progressively rename predicates while preserving states, transitions, and optimal plans. Valid LLM planning success drops from $67.5\%$ to $40.0\%$ between $0\%$ and $100\%$ renaming, while refusals remain at $0\%$. An LLM supplied with ARC's conditioning information predicts difficulty in context better than trained ARC (mean $|ρ|=0.826$). Hybrid routing between an LLM and a symbolic planner depends more on calibration to the target LLM's outcomes than on the structural score selected. Thus, established symbolic heuristics already estimate structural difficulty well; improving hybrid planning requires modeling LLM behavior sensitive to predicate semantics rather than developing more structural predictors.

title: Iterated Lavrentiev regularization under random noise: variational source conditions and rates in expectation
abstract: The convergence theory of iterated Lavrentiev regularization for nonlinear monotone ill-posed equations is deterministic: the data error is bounded by a known level that the discrepancy principle uses explicitly. Under Gaussian noise no such bound exists. For a discretized two-dimensional nonlinear inverse source problem for the Poisson equation, we analyse convergence in a finite-energy Gaussian noise model, keeping the linearized and nonlinear cases apart. For the linearized iteration the noisy and noise-free iterates differ by one resolvent applied to the noise; this gives an exact singular-value variance formula, a priori rates in expectation, and the main result: for a family of discretizations whose distance functions are bounded uniformly in the mesh, the rate is governed by that decay, which relaxes the classical range condition. The rate degrades gracefully, down to logarithmic, as the underlying continuum error loses smoothness, and a balancing rule attains it without knowing the smoothness. For the full nonlinear iteration under the order-one source condition, a truncated discrepancy principle fed only the noise level attains $σ_E^{1/2}$ in expectation, in the energy noise level $σ_E\asympσ/h$, the rare event of large noise being controlled by concentration. The rough nonlinear regime and the general-exponent nonlinear rate are left open and supported numerically for kink and jump errors. We separate the deterministic worst-case, Gaussian, and white-noise settings, prove a worst-case lower bound, and describe where the method is statistically inefficient relative to spectral cut-off. Heterogeneous media and a cost comparison with an adjoint-based scheme are given as supplementary material.

title: A noise-level-free parameter-choice rule for iterated Lavrentiev regularization of nonlinear potential monotone ill-posed problems
abstract: We consider nonlinear ill-posed operator equations $F(x)=y$ in a Hilbert space, where $F$ is monotone with a Lipschitz continuous Fréchet derivative that is self-adjoint near the solution $x^\dg$ (a locally \emph{potential} operator), and only noisy data $y^δ$ with unknown noise norm $δ:=\|y-y^δ\|$ is available. For the nonstationary iterated Lavrentiev regularization \[ x_{k+1}^δ=x_k^δ-\bigl(F'(x_k^δ)+α_kI\bigr)^{-1}\bigl(F(x_k^δ)-y^δ+α_k(x_k^δ-x_0)\bigr), \] all classical stopping rules require $δ$. We analyze a \emph{noise-level-free} parameter-choice rule of retrospective type, selecting a minimizer $k_*$ of $θ(k,y^δ)=\|F(x_k^δ)-y^δ\|^2/α_k^2$ over a finite computed window. Under a standard noise condition (necessary in view of the Bakushinskii veto) the rule is well defined and $α_{k_*}^2\ge c\,δ/\|x_0-x^\dg\|$. If moreover $x_0-x^\dg\in\R(F'(x^\dg))$ and $k_*\ge1$, we prove $\|x_{k_*}^δ-x^\dg\|=O(\sqrt{δ_*}+\sqrtδ)$ with the computable $δ_*=\|F(x_{k_*}^δ)-y^δ\|$ satisfying $κδ\leδ_*\le C\sqrtδ$, yielding the baseline rate $O(δ^{1/4})$ along admissible growing-horizon families, and $O(\sqrtδ)$ whenever $δ_*=O(δ)$; no range-invariance or tangential cone conditions are imposed. Rates under Hölder source conditions with $p\ge1$ (including saturation) follow; the case $p<1$, the removal of the self-adjointness assumption, and a full oracle inequality are identified as open problems.

title: When Weak Submodularity Meets Matroids: How Does Standard Greedy Behave?
abstract: Weakly submodular maximization finds numerous applications in machine learning, data mining and statistics. In particular, under a cardinality constraint, the standard greedy algorithm is known to attain the tight $(1-e^{-γ})$-approximation guarantee, where $γ$ denotes the submodularity ratio. However, when considering general matroid constraints, \emph{how well standard greedy can perform} has remained a longstanding open question. In this paper, we resolve this question by studying the worst-case approximation guarantee $R_{\mathrm{gr}}(γ,r)$ of standard forward greedy, where $r$ is the rank of matroid. Specifically, our first contribution is the following refined lower bound \begin{equation*} R_{\gr}(γ,r)\ge \max\left\{ \fracγ{r}, \frac{γ^2} {B_γ+\sqrt{γ(r-1)}}, \frac{γ^{r+1}} {2-γ+γ^{r+1}}, \frac{γ^2} {14\left(B_γ+\sqrt{γ(1-γ)(r-1)}\right)} \right\}, \end{equation*} where $B_γ\triangleq2-γ+γ^2$. This lower bound not only strictly improves upon the previous guarantee of $0.4γ^2/(1+\sqrt{γr})$, but also can recover the classical $1/2$-approximation guarantee at $γ=1$. Subsequently, a corresponding upper bound is established for $R_{\mathrm{gr}}(γ,r)$, namely, \begin{equation}\label{eq_upper_abstract} R_{\gr}(γ,r) \le\min\left\{\frac{1}{2},20\max\left\{\fracγ{r}, \frac{γ^2}{B_γ+ \sqrt{γ(1-γ)(r-1)}}\right\}\right\}. \end{equation} For every fixed $γ\in(0,1)$, this Eq.\eqref{eq_upper_abstract} effectively sharpens the recent $O_γ(1/\log(n-1))$ upper bound to $O_γ(r^{-1/2})$, where $n$ is the size of ground set. Putting all these results together, we eventually can obtain \[R_{\gr}(γ,r) = Θ\!\left( \max\left\{\fracγ{r}, \frac{γ^2} {1+\sqrt{γ(1-γ)r}}\right\} \right).\]

title: On $c$-Normal Maximal Chains of Sylow Subgroups in Finite Groups
abstract: Let $G$ be finite group. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is said to be $c$-normal in $G$ if there exists a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ such that $G = HN$ and $H\cap N\leq H_G$, where $H_G$ is the core of $H$ in $G$. Let $P$ be a nontrivial $p$-group. A chain of subgroups $1=P_0 <P_1<\cdots P_{n-1}<P_n=P$ is called a maximal chain of $P$ provided that $|P_i:P_{i-1}|=p$ for $i=1,2,\ldots n-1$. In this paper, we determine the structure of finite groups having $c$-normal subgroups of of a maximal chain of Sylow subgroups. We obtain new characterizations of finite $p$-nilpotent and supersolvable groups.

title: Inferring the shapes of low-mass galaxies at $z>6$ from FIREbox$^{HR}$. Where are the disks?
abstract: Context. The three-dimensional shapes of galaxies provide clues to their formation and evolution. Inferring intrinsic shapes from projected sizes and axis ratios requires assumptions about the population distribution of shape parameters. Aims. We test commonly adopted assumptions in Bayesian shape inference for high-redshift galaxies. Methods. We analyze FIREboxHR galaxies with $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)=6.5-9.5$ at $z\sim6-15$. We measure intrinsic shapes from stellar particles using the minimum covariance determinant (MCD) estimator. We also create mock JWST/NIRCam images, measure half-light radii and axis ratios, and infer intrinsic distributions from the joint distribution of projected axis ratio $q$ and size $\log a$. Results. Low-mass galaxies are predominantly prolate, with a substantial spheroidal component. Intrinsic ellipticity $E$ and triaxiality $T$ are well described by Johnson SB distributions, while intrinsic size $A$ is approximately log-normal. We therefore model $(\mathrm{logit}(E),\mathrm{logit}(T),\log A)$ with a multivariate normal distribution and allow general correlations. This model recovers the particle-measured shape distributions more faithfully than a multivariate normal model in $(E,T,\log A)$. Triaxiality-related parameters remain difficult to constrain from projected data without large samples or informative priors. Conclusions. Bayesian forward modeling can recover intrinsic shape distributions when its population model adequately describes the underlying galaxies. An unsuitable distribution can bias inferences about morphological evolution at high redshift.

title: Gaussian Lower Bounds for Distinct Subset Sums in Higher Dimensions
abstract: For sequences of $n$ nonnegative integer vectors in $\mathbb Z^k$ with distinct subset sums, we prove, for fixed $k$, the uniform lower bound $M\ge (C_k-o(1))2^{n/k}/\sqrt n$ for the largest coordinate, where \[ C_k=\sqrt{\frac{2k}π}\, \frac{(k+1)^{(k-1)/(2k)}}{\sqrt{\lfloor (k+1)^2/4\rfloor}}. \] The proof compares a Gaussian-kernel expectation with a sum over a translated lattice, uniformly over the vector sequence. We optimise the resulting quadratic-form constant using a vertex second-moment certificate. We show that $C_k$ also exceeds the variance constant obtained by optimising an ellipsoidal geometry.

title: Punctuated Equilibrium in Technological Capabilities: Commercial Selection and the Predictability of Frontier Advances
abstract: Evolutionary accounts of technological change connect new technical opportunities with economic selection. Using approximately 1.74 million electronic-component product records, we examine the tempo of capability-frontier improvement alongside the diversity of commercially offered products. In a detailed analysis of 29 manually selected capabilities, 77.8% of substantial-advance episodes consist of a single observed advance year. Across eligible three-year windows beginning with an advance, the initial observed gain accounts for an average of 79.3% of total log-capability improvement. The median share of product records near the frontier is 1.46%. Motivated by the interaction of technology push and demand pull, we extend the analysis to 204 capabilities and conduct forward out-of-sample comparisons between models using frontier history and models additionally incorporating product composition, manufacturer competition, and population dynamics. The additional indicators do not improve forecasts of subsequent frontier advances. The results document concentrated frontier gains alongside a broad distribution of commercially offered specifications. Stylized comparisons of incremental service value and switching costs identify candidate mechanisms linking application-specific valuation and production scale to the economic relevance of technical opportunities. They also specify the price, quantity, and application-level observations needed to evaluate these interpretations. We propose source-grounded, language-model-assisted extraction of demand-related information from dated external documents, with validation against independently observed market data.

title: SZED at ArGuard Shared Tasks: Multi-Task Label-Attention and Cross-Modal Fusion for Arabic Hateful Meme Detection
abstract: We present SZED's submission to ArGuard 2026 Track A: Arabic hateful meme detection. The task has two parts: binary classification (A1) and fine-grained multi-label tagging (A2). For A1, we fuse MARBERTv2 and CLIP ViT-L/14 embeddings, comparing concatenation, self-attention, and ensemble heads. For A2, we use a multi-task label-attention architecture with per-class query vectors and an auxiliary head for cascade calibration. We reach macro-F1 = 0.7597 on A1 and 0.3142 on A2 (averaged over 10 active classes). We report reproducibility across runs, per-class error patterns, and the effect of cascade calibration on the long-tailed A2 label space.

title: Anchored Exploration in Product Evolution: A Phylogenetic Network Framework for Semiconductor Designs
abstract: We develop a product phylogenetic network framework for examining anchored exploration. Using 102,465 semiconductor products grouped into 45,996 design families, we distinguish accumulated design continuity (Anchor) from externally precedented feature additions (horizontal transfer, HT). Fitted regressions yield non-monotonic relationships for HT occurrence and descendant carriage, alongside increasing within-family carriage over observed support. These patterns connect technological trajectories and recombination by distinguishing the continuity associated with incorporating external features from that associated with reproducing them in subsequent products.

title: Transformers Learn Two Competing Sorting Algorithms, and Only One Length-Generalizes
abstract: We show that two-layer transformers trained to near-zero loss on a sorting task converge to one of two mechanistically distinct solution classes depending on their initialization. One solution class consists of solutions that do not use the second attention layer to sort, but also fail to length-generalize. The other, which uses both attention layers, length-generalizes perfectly, despite only being trained to sort sequences of a fixed length. By carefully choosing the weight initialization, we demonstrate that we can steer the model toward learning one solution or the other. We identify input types that are rare at the training length but increasingly common at longer sequence lengths as a source of this disparity in length-generalization, and find that layer-wise specialization of the second class of solutions allows them to handle these rare sequences more accurately. In the second class, we discover a mechanism by which the second layer attention can use the contextual information gathered by the first layer attention to reduce its search space. On the related task of finding the minimum of a sequence, we find a similar two solution-type phenomenon, but with the opposite generalization pattern, where a different form of layer-wise specialization causes the two-layer solution to length-generalize worse than the single-attention solution.

title: A 2X2 Matrix Approach to Hopf Fibrations:: Quaternionic Reduction of Octonionic Bi-unitary Matrices and an RLLR/LRRL Bracketing Rule
abstract: We develop a common two-by-two matrix framework for the four classical Hopf fibrations associated with the real, complex, quaternionic and octonionic numbers. In all four cases the Hopf map is the image of the north pole of a sphere of trace-free Hermitian matrices under conjugation by a bi-unitary matrix, and it depends only on the first column of that matrix, without any bracketing convention, even for the non-associative octonions. Our main results concern general octonionic bi-unitary matrices, beyond the compatible matrices, with entries in a single complex subalgebra, on which earlier work on octonionic Lorentz transformations relies. We prove that every octonionic bi-unitary matrix is in fact quaternionic: its entries lie in a quaternion subalgebra depending on the matrix. We show that requiring Hermitian output leaves exactly four inequivalent ways of bracketing the octonionic triple products, among them an interlaced rule called RLLR/LRRL, and that each of them splits into an ordinary five-dimensional rotation and a four-dimensional scaling governed by a non-commutative determinant. This determines exactly when the evaluation preserves the geometry of the sphere, shows that it may contract or even collapse four dimensions, and explains why it cannot be compatible with matrix multiplication. We also recover in compact form, through the Clifford map, the known fact that suitable compatible matrices, which we interpret as transvections of the eight-sphere, generate the spin group Spin(9) by nested evaluations. Non-associativity thus does not prevent a two-by-two octonionic description of the full Spin(9) symmetry; it prevents that description from being realised through unrestricted multiplication of octonionic matrices.

title: Sharp Degree Bounds for Putinar Certificates in Terms of the Positivity Margin via Analytic Sums of Squares
abstract: We establish sharp degree bounds for Putinar sum-of-squares (SOS) certificates in terms of the positivity margin $δ$. For any fixed Archimedean quadratic module with prescribed generators and any fixed bound on the degree of the objective, we prove a uniform certificate-degree upper bound of $O(δ^{-1/2}\log^2(2/δ))$ for normalized polynomial objectives. We show that this bound is sharp by constructing a matching lower-bound example in three variables, thereby establishing that the dependence on $δ$ is optimal. These matching bounds also yield sharp worst-case convergence rates for the Lasserre hierarchy.

title: Polynomial Spectral Gap Estimates for Finitely Differentiable Quasi-Periodic Schrödinger Operators
abstract: We prove polynomial upper bounds on spectral gaps of quasi-periodic Schrödinger operators with small $C^{k}$ potentials and Diophantine frequencies. For sufficiently large $k$, the decay exponent is $k-34τ$, where $τ$ is the Diophantine exponent. We construct examples with lower bounds along infinitely many gap labels, showing that the leading coefficient $1$ of $k$ is asymptotically optimal. The proof uses quantitative reducibility and the Moser-Pöschel argument.

title: Convex-cyclic and super convex-cyclic weighted shifts
abstract: Convex-cyclic operators are considered by H. Rezaei \cite{R1}. However, there is a general lack of theoretical understanding of super convex-cyclic operators. In this paper, we analyze super convex-cyclic operators. In particular, Super Convex-cyclicity Criterion is described. Additionally, we characterize convex-cyclicity of (invertible) bilateral weighted shifts in terms of their weight sequences, which in turn correct \cite[H. Rezaei (2013) Theorem 4.2 ]{R1}. Meanwhile, we give super convex-cyclicity of (invertible) weighted shifts in the bilateral case.

title: Latent Projection for Latent Planning
abstract: Latent world models let an agent plan in latent space. The planner searches for an action sequence that minimizes a cost, and that cost is often the $\ell_2$ distance between the predicted terminal latent and the goal latent. The latent, however, is partly noise: the regularizer that prevents collapse during world model training promotes variance in the directions carrying no signal. We show that the same regularizer also supplies the structure to prune that noise in the latent. SIGReg drives the latent marginal to a standard Gaussian at every step, and assuming further that the latent sequence is a Gauss-Markov process, the transition is linear with its covariance pinned by the map itself, $z' \mid z \sim \mathcal{N}(Az,\, I - AA^\top)$. Fitting the state dynamics $A$ therefore yields the covariance at no additional cost, and in its eigenbasis each latent direction carries its own uncertainty. Furthermore, constraining $A$ to be a normal matrix fixes that basis across timesteps, so one eigenbasis measures the uncertainty over an arbitrary number of steps and serves as a stable basis to compute the planning cost on. We then restrict the $\ell_2$ cost to the $k$-dimensional subspace the state dynamics carry forward with the least uncertainty. The correction is post hoc: the encoder, the predictor, the rollout, and the planner are all left untouched, and only a single constrained matrix, $A$, is fit. We evaluate across six environments and show large gains on the 2D navigation tasks, TwoRoom and PointMaze, raising success rate over the plain $\ell_2$ cost by up to $+54.7$ points under a harder planning setting. Code is available at https://github.com/yjang43/lp2.

title: Elementary-Symmetric Ricci Gravity: Metric Formulation
abstract: We investigate a four-dimensional metric theory of gravity whose Lagrangian is a linear combination of the elementary symmetric polynomials of the Ricci tensor. We derive the field equations and characterize Einstein vacua and a real, diagonalizable class of parallel-Ricci vacua. The latter includes direct products of two constant-curvature surfaces and can exhibit a hierarchy of curvature radii. The Einstein vacua possess multiple branches associated with the distinct roots of a polynomial, whose multiple roots define boundaries in parameter space. We derive the linearized equations on maximally symmetric backgrounds, distinguish the scalar and spin-2 degrees of freedom, and then analyze their classical linear stability. We also obtain the generalized Friedmann constraint and the associated homogeneous evolution equations. An illustrative spatially flat solution evolves from the neighborhood of an unstable de Sitter solution toward a stable de Sitter solution. This behavior may motivate further investigation into early- and late-time accelerated expansion and provide a gravity-driven mechanism for automatic end of inflation.

title: Rotating Barrow entropy-inspired wormholes versus black holes: null trajectories, shadow morphology, and exotic matter
abstract: We construct a rotating traversable wormhole supported by a regular, entropy-inspired matter distribution and investigate its geometry, null geodesics, shadow morphology, and exotic matter content. We derive the geometry from the Barrow deformation of the Bekenstein--Hawking area law, characterized by an exponent $0<n\le1$, which replaces point-like divergences with a regular matter profile. The resulting energy density is negative everywhere and scales as $ρ_B\propto-r^{-n-3}$, while the shape function smoothly satisfies the flare-out condition at the throat. We introduce slow rotation via $N(r,θ)=\exp[αJ^2\cos^2θ/r^2]$ and $ω(r)=2J/r^3$; both remain finite at the throat, ensuring a horizon-free, traversable geometry. Equatorial null geodesics yield a photon-sphere condition distinct from the standard black-hole relation. In the static limit, the photon sphere sits at the throat, $r_{\rm ph}=r_{\rm th}$; for slow rotation, the prograde branch moves to $r_{\rm ph}^2\simeq 6J$, while the retrograde branch is pushed toward the throat. The critical impact parameters are $\mathscr{B}_{\pm}\approx\pm r_{\rm ph}+2J/r_{\rm ph}$. For $M=1$, $r_{\rm th}=1$, $J/M^2=0.5$, this gives $r_{\rm ph}\approx1.732$, $\mathscr{B}_{+}\approx1.90$, $\mathscr{B}_{-}\approx-1.55$, and a fractional asymmetry $\mathcal{A}\approx0.10$. The weak and null energy conditions are violated, with the strongest violation near the throat, while the Barrow exponent controls the localization of exotic matter. The volume-integral quantifier $I_V$ remains finite when $r_{\rm th}^{n+1}=4M/[(n+2)π^{n/2}]$. Comparisons with Kerr and regular black holes indicate that shadow diameter alone may be degenerate, whereas photon-ring structure and rotational asymmetry provide complementary signatures capable of distinguishing this entropy-inspired wormhole from black-hole alternatives.

title: Zeeman Quantum Geometry of the Layer Pseudo-spin
abstract: Two-dimensional layers coupled by position-dependent interlayer tunnelling host a layer pseudo-spin whose polarization is a controllable internal degree of freedom. We introduce the quantum geometry of this layer pseudo-spin: a mixed tensor formed from the interband Berry connection and the layer matrix element, which governs the response to an oscillating in-plane electric field. Because the layer pseudo-spin is an Ising-type scalar invariant under threefold rotation, its selection rules differ from those of a pseudovector spin. In a minimal two-band model, the layer-pseudo-spin quantum metric and Zeeman--Berry curvature are nonzero, while their zone integrals vanish. An in-plane drive therefore leaves the spatially averaged polarization unchanged at linear order but imprints a moiré-periodic intracell pattern, directly imageable by layer-resolved tunnelling. For twisted MoTe$_2$ bilayer, we quantify the local dipole modulation and identify the rectified, helicity-odd, and third-harmonic channels through which a net response appears at higher order.

title: Uniqueness of twisted linear periods
abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero, and let $\D$ be either $F$ or a quaternion division algebra over $F$. We prove that every irreducible smooth representation of $\GL_{p+q}(\D)$ has at most one linear period transforming under any prescribed character of $\GL_p(\D)\times\GL_q(\D)$.

title: Load-Balanced Neural-Network-Aided Adaptive Tabulation of Phase Equilibria for Transcritical Multiphase Flows
abstract: Simulating high-pressure transcritical flows with phase change is critical for advanced propulsion, yet traditional first-principles approaches, vapor-liquid equilibrium (VLE) calculations, consume most of the runtime and frequently fail to converge. Standalone machine learning models introduce heavy evaluation overhead across large grids, while dynamic tabulation still relies on fragile iterative solvers. To resolve these limitations, this study introduces a hybrid In-Situ Adaptive Tabulation and Artificial Neural Network (ISAT-ANN) framework. A pre-trained ANN replaces the iterative solver during table expansion to guarantee crash-free operation, while ISAT enables rapid data retrieval via local linear interpolation. To eliminate parallel load imbalances, an O(N) greedy load-balancing algorithm redistributes computational tasks across cores. Coupled with Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR), the framework was validated on a Mach 5 shock-droplet interaction benchmark. It accurately captured shock-interface dynamics without instability, achieving a 2.30 times speedup in thermodynamic calculations on a single core and 2.62 times in parallel over standalone ANNs, with AMR providing an additional 2.92 times overall efficiency boost. This plug-and-play framework offers a stable, scalable path for high-fidelity multiphase flow simulations.

title: Migrate Computation, Not Data: Fault Recovery in Neuromorphic Many-Core Systems
abstract: As neuromorphic systems scale to thousands of near-memory cores, aging-induced permanent faults in neuron-update datapaths become an important obstacle to long-term deployment. Existing online recovery methods typically retire a faulty core and migrate its neurons, along with their weights and membrane states, to healthy cores. This whole-core treatment incurs high recovery traffic and makes recovery depend on scarce destinations; at high utilization, there may be enough surviving compute capacity but insufficient free storage to copy the affected neuron context. This paper presents SpikeRelay, an online recovery framework for diagnosed compute-unit faults. SpikeRelay exploits the fact that, in many neuromorphic cores, the compute datapath, local SRAM, and router are distinct modules: a compute fault need not destroy stored weights and states or disconnect the core from the NoC. Instead of retiring a faulty core and migrating its neuron data, SpikeRelay converts the faulty core into a storage-and-forwarding node while offloading neuron-update computation to a healthy rescue core. This decoupling of storage and computation eliminates recovery-time data migration and greatly reduces spare-SRAM requirements. Consequently, SpikeRelay sustains 100\% recovery at 92.2\% SRAM utilization and a 50\% fault rate, whereas the best baseline achieves only 22.1\%.

title: Think Before You Transcribe: Context-Steered Reasoning for Hotword-Aware Speech Recognition
abstract: Contextual automatic speech recognition (ASR) improves rare-entity recognition by supplying candidate hotwords, but retrieved candidates may be incomplete or incorrect. A reliable system must therefore exploit a relevant candidate without allowing unsupported alternatives to override the acoustic evidence. We propose a context-steered reasoning framework that generates a short, audio-grounded caption before transcription. This task-specific representation lets the model assess candidate relevance before making a lexical decision. Supervised fine-tuning establishes the structured caption-to-transcription behavior, while targeted trajectory injection strengthens group relative policy optimization when difficult utterances yield only unsuccessful rollouts. Experiments across diverse context conditions show that the proposed method consistently improves both transcription quality and hotword recognition while remaining robust to irrelevant candidates.

title: Dynamic Dual-Feedback Conformal Inference for Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Quantifying uncertainty in time series forecasting is particularly demanding because sequential data exhibit temporal dependence and are prone to distributional changes. Conformal inference has emerged as a powerful uncertainty quantification approach through the construction of prediction sets. Recent advances have introduced online conformal methods that adaptively adjust prediction thresholds through feedback mechanisms. However, the existing feedback mechanism typically relies solely on miscoverage indicators (actual feedback), whether the true label falls within the interval at each time step, while overlooking the empirical prediction threshold (estimated feedback) that is derived from the oracle conformal method. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Dual-feedback Conformal Inference (DDCI), which incorporates a dual-feedback mechanism consisting of actual feedback and estimated feedback. The former drives the primary adjustment of the intervals based on true observations, while the latter dampens excessive expansions or contractions by leveraging empirical thresholds from conformal inference during updates. By balancing these two signals, DDCI achieves more stable and narrower prediction intervals in sequential settings while maintaining near-nominal coverage in practice.

title: REST: Reliability-Guided Spatial Transcriptomics Supervision for Gene Expression Prediction from Histopathological HE-Stained Images
abstract: Histopathology is central to cancer diagnosis, but morphology in Hematoxylin and Eosin (HE)-stained images does not directly reveal the molecular states that characterize disease heterogeneity and inform tumor characterization, prognostic assessment, and biomarker discovery. Spatial Transcriptomics (ST) measures spatially resolved gene expression, providing molecular information within tissue architecture, yet differences in assay coverage and spot informativeness make paired HE--ST observations unequally reliable for representation learning. We propose Reliability-Guided Spatial Transcriptomics (REST) supervision with Biological Program Bank (BPB), a program-structured and reliability-guided ST-supervised training framework for predicting molecular information from H\&E images. REST constructs BPB from curated signature, pathway, and cell-type gene sets to provide a shared structure for ST encoding, reliability estimation, and molecular reconstruction. Guided by BPB, Spot-Reliability Contrastive Alignment (SRCA) measures the reliability of each spot from assay-level program coverage and spot-level activity dispersion, and reweights HE--ST alignment accordingly. Biology-Informed Program Reconstruction (BIPR) further uses learnable program queries to reconstruct member-gene expression from histological morphology. REST's training corpus comprised 209 samples (407,475 spots across 16 organs); evaluation used 70 disjoint samples (230,056 spots across eight organs) for gene-expression, pathway-activity, and cell-signature prediction. REST achieved the highest Macro correlation among state-of-the-art ST-supervised training methods and outperformed existing pathology foundation models. Code is available at https://github.com/lanfz2000/REST.

title: k-Submodular Cover Problem with a Matroid Constraint
abstract: We investigate k-submodular cover problem with a matroid constraint on an n-element ground set V , which seeks k disjoint subsets of V with minimal cost, where their union is an independent set for some matroid defined on V and the k-submodular utility function surpasses a specified threshold. This problem generalizes the k-submodular cover problem and has a wide range of applications in artificial intelligence and combinatorial optimization. In this paper, we propose a matroid extended greedy algorithm for this problem, analyze its bi-criteria approximation ratio, and further derive an improved approximation ratio under the special case of unit costs.

title: Euclid Bypass end-to-end simulations for spectroscopic galaxy clustering performance assessment
abstract: We present a simulation framework for Euclid galaxy clustering measurements that reproduces the essential behaviour of the spectroscopic reduction chain, bypassing the computation required by full pixel-level simulations. The framework comprises two complementary tools, FastSpec, which simulates 1-dimensional slitless spectra with a simplified instrument and noise model, and Pypelid, which computes detection probabilities on input catalogues, accounting for the survey dithering sequence and spatially varying noise. We develop calibrated prescriptions for the survey selection function, redshift errors, and redshift interloper populations. Applied to the Euclid Wide Survey, the baseline selection yields a redshift purity of 74% and a sample completeness of 45%, which improves with the use of Euclid photometric colours. The redshift error distribution is found to have a Gaussian core of width $σ_z = 9.4 \times 10^{-4}$, with no significant trend over $0.9 < z < 1.8$. Emission lines [OIII]5008 and [SIII]9530 misidentified as H$α$ contribute a few to ten per cent depending on redshift, while catastrophic redshift measurement failures dominate at low signal-to-noise ratio. Simulating the Data Release 1 footprint, we find that complex survey selection effects can be corrected with a forward-modelled random catalogue, recovering the monopole and quadrupole of the galaxy 2-point correlation function. The simplified noise model does not include residual contamination from overlapping spectra, or other artefacts seen in early Euclid data; this will be revisited with DR1 data. The framework provides an efficient route for characterising the Euclid spectroscopic selection function at the precision required for galaxy clustering science, and is the basis for systematic error assessments in Euclid galaxy clustering analyses.

title: 3D-MoE: Complementarity-Guided Hardware-Software Co-Design for MoE Decode on 3D-Stacked NMP
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) have become a mainstream way to scale Large Language Models (LLMs), because each token activates only a small subset of experts, reducing inference cost. However, MoE decode remains highly memory-bound and exhibits strongly skewed, time-varying expert loads. 3D-stacked DRAM near-memory processing (NMP) provides the bandwidth that decode demands, yet its tiled organization makes load balancing expensive: expert parallelism (EP) preserves locality but suffers from hotspot-induced imbalance, while more distributed strategies weaken locality and increase NoC traffic. To address this locality-balance conflict, we observe that domain-specialized token routing creates offsetting expert-load fluctuations across decode steps, a property we call expert complementarity. Using this insight, we propose 3D-MoE, a hardware--software co-designed system for MoE decode on 3D-stacked NMP. 3D-MoE uses offline, one-time complementarity-guided grouping and locality-aware mapping to establish coarse-grained inter-group balance, handles residual intra-group hotspots through a lightweight Collaborative Memory-Network (CMN) that streams each hot expert's weight tiles once from its host DRAM channel to helper cores over a reconfigured local broadcast path, and uses cost-aware online remapping to remain robust to workload drift. Across MoE models, 3D-MoE achieves an average 4.63$\times$ MoE-layer speedup over EP and improves end-to-end throughput by 1.58$\times$--1.86$\times$ over the strongest NMP baselines, with 2.11\% additional logic-die area.

title: CoASFL: Coupled Consistency Optimization for Asynchronous Split Federated Learning
abstract: Split Federated Learning (SFL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for training large-scale deep models on resource-constrained edge devices. Although asynchronous SFL alleviates the straggler bottleneck caused by system heterogeneity, it inevitably introduces two coupled dimensions of inconsistency: horizontal inconsistency across clients and vertical inconsistency between clients and the server. These inconsistencies, further exacerbated by statistical heterogeneity, result in biased activation representations, model divergence, and severe client drift. To address these challenges, we propose CoASFL, an inconsistency-aware asynchronous SFL framework that incorporates a dynamic activation merging mechanism and a consistency-aware model aggregation mechanism. Specifically, CoASFL constructs more consistent activation sequences from heterogeneous clients to alleviate horizontal inconsistency, and dynamically adjusts aggregation weights according to client participation frequencies and progress gaps to mitigate vertical inconsistency. By jointly coordinating activation-level and model-level consistency, CoASFL effectively suppresses inconsistency propagation during asynchronous training. Extensive experiments on an 80-device heterogeneous edge testbed demonstrate that CoASFL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art SFL approaches, accelerating training by 1.61$\times$ to 3.74$\times$ and improving final model accuracy by up to 3.26\% under heterogeneous scenarios.

title: TRACE: Training-aware Robustness and Challenge Evaluation for Text-Vision Embedding Models
abstract: Existing benchmarks for text-vision embedding models report aggregate scores that obscure whether performance comes from general capabilities, task-specific adaptation, or robustness to challenging tasks. We introduce TRACE, a Training-aware Robustness and Challenge Evaluation framework that reorganizes 168 tasks from various sources of datasets into three categories: General, Adaptability, and Challenge. Through controlled experiments on two text-vision embedding models, we show that combining general and adaptation data improves Adaptability performance by 7.67 and 7.09 points, respectively, while largely preserving General performance. However, Challenge performance remains below 5.0, with limited improvements from additional training data. Further analysis identifies multilingual and visual-document tasks as major weaknesses. Our findings demonstrate that data adaptation alone is insufficient to address these challenges, highlighting the need for methodological advances beyond data-centric improvements.

title: How to get the best and fairest performance out of your ASR system using activation steering
abstract: Activation steering for ASR systems is an underexplored technique in improving both ASR performance and demographic fairness. We investigate two forms of activation steering: paired activation subtraction, and supervised optimization. We find the former to be ineffective at ameliorating ASR performance whatsoever, while the latter is quite effective at deriving steering vectors (SVs) that improve at once overall ASR performance and demographic fairness along such diverse axes as gender, age, and dialect. We also explore what types of data---from the most to the least personal---are necessary for calculating or training SVs. First, we show significant performance in performance from training SVs using an eclectic group of speakers from the same dataset. Furthermore, we find that vectors trained using acoustically similar speakers leads to ASR performances that are competitive or superior to vectors trained on the same speaker, or speakers from the same labeled demographic group. This finding shows that we can harness activation steering for few-shot adaptation given access to a speaker's demography, or zero-shot adaptation to unseen speakers without the need for any labels at all.

title: SPEM: Structure-Aware Procedural Memory for Efficient Skill Use in LLM Agents
abstract: LLM-based agents increasingly rely on reusable skills. However, scaling skill libraries makes efficient and accurate skill use difficult. Full skill loading incurs high token and runtime overhead. In contrast, flat semantic retrieval treats skills as independent text entries, ignoring dependencies, execution order, state transitions, and data flow constraints. We propose SPEM, a lightweight structure-aware procedural memory framework for efficient skill use in LLM-based agents. SPEM maintains Atomic Skill Memory for individual skills and Skill-DAG Memory for reusable compositions derived from successful executions. For a new task, SPEM reuses high-confidence Skill-DAG templates when available. Otherwise, it retrieves atomic skills and invokes Skill-GNN for state- and structure-aware skill selection. Successful executions are written back as new Skill-DAGs, allowing procedural memory to accumulate over time. Experiments on ALFWorld and SkillsBench show that SPEM achieves the best overall effectiveness--efficiency trade-off, reaching 87.1% ALFWorld success and 38.38% SkillsBench reward while reducing token and runtime costs against strong baselines.

title: Tailoring Dielectric Relaxation and Charge Transport in Amorphous Ge-Te-Se Phase-Change Materials through Yttrium Incorporation
abstract: The Te(1-x)(GeSe0.5)Yx (x = 0.05, 0.10, 0.15) alloys were prepared by a melt-quenching method and characterized using dielectric spectroscopy. The dielectric parameters and electrical conductivity were evaluated to assess their potential for phase-change memory and other electronic applications. The temperature and frequency dependence of the dielectric constants, ac conductivity, and dielectric loss of prepared chalcogenide glassy alloys were investigated over the frequency range 1 Hz - 1 MHz, and the temperature range 302 - 422 K, below the glass transition temperature. Both dielectric loss and dielectric constant were found to decrease with increasing frequency and decreasing temperature. The observed dielectric loss change was interpreted using the Guintini model of dielectric dispersion, correlated barrier hopping (CBH) model, and orientation polarization. The Cole-Cole analysis confirmed a distribution of relaxation times and yielded activation energies consistent with the CBH conduction mechanism. The frequency dependence of the ac conductivity follows the power law (Aωs), where the frequency exponent (s < 1) decreases with increasing temperature, further supporting the CBH conduction mechanism. The incorporation of Y increases the density of localized tail states, resulting in enhanced ac conductivity. These findings suggest that the investigated materials are promising candidates for future phase-change memory and other electronic device applications.

title: Achieving ultrahigh-temperature superfluidity in atomic Fermi gases by suppressing pairing fluctuations
abstract: Achieving room-temperature superconductivity has been a long-sought goal of both the physics community and the industry. The superfluid transition temperature $T_\mathrm{c}$ of a Fermi system initially increases with increasing pairing strength between fermions following the mean-field prediction of the Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) theory, and is then suppressed by pairing fluctuations as the strength increases further, which prevents $T_\mathrm{c}$ from becoming high. Here we propose a mechanism for suppressing pairing fluctuations using the synergy between population imbalance and momentum space confinement in lattice systems, enabling an ultrahigh $T_\mathrm{c}$ at moderately strong attraction. We show that in a three-dimensional optical lattice, strong Pauli exclusion between paired and excess majority fermions pushes up the pair excitation energy and suppresses finite-momentum pairing fluctuations. The mechanism is general to any lattice with a finite Brillouin zone; the optimal imbalance is modest ($p\lesssim 0.1$), keeping the Zeeman field small and avoiding orbital complications. The gapped pair dispersion at moderate imbalance exponentially suppresses thermal condensate depletion, providing a testable signature. The gapped dispersion, enhanced condensate fraction, and pseudogap reduction are all accessible in present-day experiments. This work opens new avenues toward room-temperature superconductivity.

title: A Critical Case for the Near Field Refraction Problem in Negative Refractive Index Material
abstract: This paper studies the near field refraction problem for the critical case in negative refractive index material. Snell law in vector form is first reviewed, and the physical constraint governing refraction is discussed. We then define the refractor for the critical case and analyze several of its key properties. Building on these properties, we introduce the notion of a weak solution to this problem and prove the existence of the weak solution when the target measure is either discrete or a finite Radon measure. The proof relies on the Minkowski method, an iterative approach to refraction and reflection problems in geometric optics.

title: CorteXforge: Scenario-Based RF Dataset Generation on Real Testbeds
abstract: Deep learning for radio frequency (RF) signal analysis relies on large annotated datasets, yet synthetic datasets trade physical realism for controllability, while uncontrolled over-theair measurements offer realism but limited reproducibility. We present CorteXforge, a scenario-based framework for generating realistic and reproducible RF datasets on programmable software defined radio (SDR) testbeds. High-level RF scenarios are automatically translated into synchronized experiments executed on the SLICES-RI/CorteXlab platform, producing fully annotated Signal Metadata Format (SIGMF) datasets that capture hardware impairments and propagation effects. We validate CorteXforge through automatic modulation classification using ModForge, an over-the-air (OTA) dataset generated with the framework. Cross-domain experiments reveal a synthetic-to-real performance gap and show that synthetic pretraining remains beneficial for adaptation to OTA data. CorteXforge provides a practical foundation for reproducible RF dataset generation and future research on domain generalization.

title: ORBIT: Autoregressive Time Series Generation via Next Frequency-Band Prediction
abstract: Deep generative models provide an effective modern solution to alleviating the problem of data scarcity by synthesizing realistic time series. However, despite the considerable progress achieved by existing deep time series generators, two key challenges remain: (1) learning hierarchical representations for heterogeneous temporal patterns; and (2) coordinating the generation process of heterogeneous temporal dynamics. To address these key bottlenecks, in this work, we propose ORBIT, a unified deep generative framework for time series. Specifically, we develop two key components: the Frequency-Hierarchical VQ-VAE (FH-VQ-VAE) and the Frequency-Band Autoregressive Transformer (FBAR). The former learns hierarchical representations by decomposing latent temporal representations into different frequency bands and applying residual quantization with increasing token budgets. The latter establishes a novel low-to-high frequency autoregressive direction, yielding a time series generation process that first constructs global temporal structures and then incrementally incorporates fine-grained temporal details. These compact designs not only disentangle heterogeneous temporal patterns for more effective representation learning but also mitigate potential interference among different temporal dynamics during generation. Extensive experiments on multiple challenging real-world benchmarks demonstrate that ORBIT achieves state-of-the-art overall performance while exhibiting superior inference efficiency compared with advanced baselines.

title: HierDTA: Hierarchical Structure-Aware Representation Learning for Drug--Target Affinity Prediction
abstract: Drug--target affinity (DTA) prediction plays an important role in computer-aided drug discovery, where reliable computational models can help prioritize compound--protein pairs before experimental validation. A key challenge in DTA prediction is to effectively mine multi-level molecular information from drug structures while accurately modeling the binding-site environment of target proteins. To address these issues, we introduce HierDTA, a hierarchical structure-aware framework for DTA prediction. \textcolor{black}{HierDTA represents each drug as an atom--motif heterogeneous graph and introduces an augmentation module that propagates functional-motif semantics to the corresponding atoms. For proteins, kinase-domain structures are converted into residue interaction graphs. The resulting atom and residue representations are integrated using cross-attention to capture pair-specific relationships, while molecule fingerprints and pretrained ESM-2 embeddings provide complementary global information. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, HierDTA achieves superior performance on the Davis dataset across all metrics and attains the highest \(r_m^2\) of 0.791 on KIBA. It also exhibits strong generalization under cold-start settings, particularly on KIBA, where MSE is reduced by 21.7\% in the unseen-protein scenario. Ablation study and interpretability analysis supported the contributions of the hierarchical augmentation and interaction components.} Case studies further showed that HierDTA provided early enrichment of candidate bioactive compounds. These results indicate that HierDTA is an effective framework for affinity prediction and target-specific virtual screening.

title: Evaluating Tibetan Speech Recognition Across Dialects and Adaptation Regimes: A Multi-Granularity Analysis
abstract: Tibetan speech recognition is usually evaluated with character or syllable error rates because the writing system does not mark word boundaries. These metrics can rank systems differently and respond differently to adaptation failures. We combine character error rate, syllable error rate, and segmented word error rate in one evaluation framework. We use dictionary-based, neural, and language-model-based segmentation and compare their boundaries with expert annotations. We evaluate five ASR architectures on Lhasa Tibetan, then test zero-shot transfer and target-corpus adaptation on five additional corpus subsets. We also vary LoRA rank and training-data size to examine adaptation failure. The results show that a lower character error does not always lead to a lower syllable or segmented-word error. These ranking differences persist across corpora. Metric correlations also weaken in some unsuccessful adaptation settings. Higher LoRA ranks improve syllable and segmented-word scores but remain worse than full fine-tuning in the tested range. A standardized phonological representation provides another view of spelling errors. These findings support evaluation at several linguistic levels and motivate better segmentation and adaptation methods for low-resource ASR.

title: Replan for Error Recovery: Training Embodied VLMs through Verifiable Interaction with Action-Grouped Turn-GSPO
abstract: Embodied VLMs can execute increasingly complex manipulation tasks, yet execution errors can leave the environment in states that require replanning for recovery. Existing recovery methods either rely on inference-time mechanisms with fixed policies or learn from failure examples and reference corrections rather than verified action outcomes. To enable recovery learning through verifiable interaction, we introduce the Embodied Replanning for Recovery Environment (ERR-Env), which provides feedback on task progress and execution errors. We further construct ERR-Bench, a benchmark with held-out tasks spanning nominal, intermediate, and error states for evaluating recovery capability and execution reliability. We then propose Action-Grouped Turn-GSPO (AGT-GSPO), an online reinforcement learning method combining turn-level rewards for task progress and error states with action-grouped advantage estimation, and use it to train ERR-VLM, a compact 2B embodied VLM. Evaluation on ERR-Bench reveals a mismatch between task progress and execution reliability across diverse VLMs. AGT-GSPO improves ERR-VLM by 10.25 percentage points in Strict Success Rate for error-free completion and 22.95 percentage points in Recovery Rate, while ablations and zero-shot transfer further validate the effectiveness of our method.

title: Endpoint maximal estimates for the half-wave propagator
abstract: We present a proof of the strong maximal estimate for the Euclidean half-wave propagator at the critical pair $s_d=d/(d+1)$ and $q_d=2(d+1)/(d-1)$, in every dimension $d\ge2$, i.e. \begin{equation*} \biggl\|\sup_{0<t<1}|e^{it\sqrt{-Δ}}f(x)|\biggl\|_{L^{q_d}({\mathbb{R}}^d)} \le C_d\|f\|_{ H^{s_d}({\mathbb{R}}^d)}. \end{equation*}

title: PSR~B0355+54: An Unexpected Compendium of Nearly All Scintillation Arc Morphologies
abstract: Scintillation arcs are sensitive probes of multipath propagation, offering a window into the distribution of scattering material in the interstellar medium. Contrary to the common observational finding that individual pulsars exhibit only a limited range of scintillation arc morphologies, we report that PSR~B0355+54, observed simultaneously at 2.25/8.60~GHz with the Shanghai Tianma Radio Telescope, displays nearly the full range of known arc patterns, many of which evolve rapidly. Across 54 observations from 2020 to 2026, we detect scintillation arcs in 53/53 usable observations at 2.25~GHz and 33/49 at 8.60~GHz. At 2.25~GHz, the secondary spectra exhibit five broad morphological types: forward arcs, inverted arclets, diffuse arcs, diffuse power, and irregular structures, with prominent displaced arclets appearing in several observations. In contrast, the 8.60-GHz spectra are generally dominated by faint forward arcs. Despite these marked morphological differences, the scaled curvatures and their annual variations agree between the two frequencies, showing that both trace the same dominant scattering screen at a fractional distance of $s=0.069^{+0.015}_{-0.014}$ near the pulsar, further supporting a possible association with the \ion{H}{ii} region Sh~2-205. Simulations show that this diversity can arise from variations in the scattered-image distribution within this screen, while brightness reconstructions at 2.25~GHz resolve localized structure down to $\sim0.02~\mathrm{mas}$. Tracking four arclets over 10~h at 8.60~GHz, including two displaced arclets, reveals a common evolutionary trend consistent with the line of sight sweeping across small-scale scattering structure, helping explain the rapid arc evolution.

title: Axion-Like Particle Searches at Muon Colliders: Photon-Neutrino Signatures and Heavy-Neutral-Lepton Feasibility
abstract: We study the mono-photon signature $μ^+μ^-\toγa\toγν\barν$ at $3$ and $10\TeV$ muon colliders, with integrated luminosities of $1$ and $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, in a two-coupling axion-like-particle (ALP) simplified model. Five benchmarks spanning $m_a=100$--$1000\GeV$ are generated at $g_{aγγ}=0.01\TeV^{-1}$ and flavor-universal pseudoscalar neutrino couplings $y_ν=0.1$ or $0.3$, giving invisible branching fractions above 99.995\% and mono-photon cross sections of $0.00854$--$0.01217\,\mathrm{fb}$. Assuming a 1\% background normalization uncertainty, a cut-based photon-line selection gives projected 95\% sensitivity to $g_{aγγ}\simeq0.039$--$0.045\TeV^{-1}$ at $3\TeV$ and $0.0137$--$0.0140\TeV^{-1}$ at $10\TeV$. A ROOT/TMVA gradient-boosted decision tree with validation-fixed thresholds reaches held-out AUC values of $0.9967$--$0.9993$ and $g_{95}=0.0192$--$0.0400\TeV^{-1}$ at $3\TeV$ and $0.0122$--$0.0144\TeV^{-1}$ at $10\TeV$. Because only 2-41 irreducible-background test events populate the optimized classifier tails, the mass--coupling contours are reported as projected expected sensitivities rather than profile-likelihood or CL$_s$ exclusions. A separate appendix records a phenomenological, parton-level HNL diphoton feasibility study; it is not used to claim detector-level sensitivity or exclusion.} \keywords{Axion-like particles, muon collider, mono-photon, diphoton, heavy neutral leptons, neutrinos, multivariate analysis, effective field theory

title: An Algebraic Formulation of Thermality in Nested Rindler Wedges
abstract: Padmanabhan and Kolekar had demonstrated the phenomenon of recursive thermality in two dimensional free field theories where the Rindler vacuum appears thermal to an observer accelerated with respect to the Rindler observer. We study the same construction at an algebraic level for conformal field theories. At each step, a parent wedge is conformally mapped to a reference Minkowski spacetime, where a new right Rindler wedge and its left sibling are selected. We illustrate that under the Bisognano--Wichmann property, thermality holds at every generation: the state associated with a parent wedge becomes a KMS state when restricted to its right child. Further, using the modular structure of the wedge and its causal sibling, we identify the sibling algebra with the modular commutant and derive the corresponding recursive modular flow explicitly.

title: Least singular values of Gaussian matrices with deterministic shifts
abstract: Let $A$ be a deterministic real square matrix and $G$ a standard Gaussian matrix. We determine $\E\smin(A+G)$, up to universal constants, in terms of the singular values of $A$. The expectation is comparable to the square root of the smallest zero of the expected characteristic polynomial of $(A+G)^{\top}(A+G)$. This resolves Problem~3 in Tikhomirov's ICM 2022 survey. We also prove that the zeros of the expected characteristic polynomial are majorized by the expected ordered eigenvalues of $(A+G)^{\top}(A+G)$.

title: Gamma-ray Bursts as Cosmological Probes Calibrated with Strongly Lensed Quasars and Neural Networks
abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) extend distance measurements to redshifts beyond those routinely probed by Type Ia supernovae, but their use in cosmology is limited by calibration circularity and possible redshift-dependent effects. We investigate strongly lensed quasars as external calibrators of the Amati and Combo GRB relations. We reconstruct the luminosity-distance relation using an artificial neural network trained on TDCOSMO strong-lensing distances, with the absolute scale inherited from the lensing-only calibration. To avoid extrapolation, only GRBs within the lens-supported redshift interval are used for calibration. We then infer cosmological parameters through a hierarchical Bayesian analysis of flat $Λ$CDM, with $w_0w_a$CDM examined as a consistency test. For flat $Λ$CDM, Amati yields $H_0=78.26^{+17.87}_{-16.30}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $Ω_m=0.670^{+0.223}_{-0.276}$, while Combo yields $H_0=78.71^{+13.83}_{-11.29}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $Ω_m=0.635^{+0.235}_{-0.242}$. Amati is relatively insensitive to the phenomenological redshift term, whereas Combo shows a stronger dependence. Injection--recovery tests indicate that an unmodelled positive Combo trend can bias $H_0$ and $Ω_m$ upward. Strong-lens calibration therefore offers a route to extending the GRB Hubble diagram, but the inferred $H_0$ is not an independent GRB measurement: it retains the TDCOSMO distance scale. The precision is limited by GRB scatter, redshift-dependent systematics, and lens-modelling uncertainties.

title: Robust Latent Variable Graphical Models: Exact Recovery and Fundamental Limits
abstract: We study robust estimation of a Gaussian precision matrix that decomposes as a sparse matrix minus a symmetric, possibly indefinite, low-rank matrix, a structure that arises when latent-variable marginalization is combined with conditioning on linear measurements. The proposed convex estimator replaces the sample covariance by the centered Gaussian measure-transformed (MT) covariance, which preserves the signed graph of the sparse component under the nominal model, and penalizes the low-rank component by the nuclear norm of a congruence transform, an atomic norm that encodes structural side information. Our main result is a primal--dual witness theorem: under restricted invertibility and irrepresentability conditions on the Fisher information, the raw convex optimizer is unique, has no false edges, recovers the signs of all sufficiently strong edges, and has exactly the true rank and inertia. These conditions reduce to the graphical-lasso conditions when the low-rank part is absent, and we verify them from primitive incoherence and near-isotropy assumptions. Over a class on which they hold uniformly, we prove information-theoretic limits for Frobenius estimation, signed graph recovery, and inertia recovery. In particular, inertia recovery requires $N\gtrsim p/ν_{\min}^2$ samples, where $ν_{\min}$ is the smallest nonzero eigenvalue modulus of the low-rank part; the spectral beta-min condition of the witness theorem is necessary up to a $\sqrt{\log p}$ factor; and the Frobenius risk attains the minimax rate up to a factor $\sqrt{μ(1+\min\{d,r\})\log p}$, where $μ$ is the incoherence parameter, $d$ the maximal degree, and $r$ the rank. We further quantify robustness under Huber contamination, with a bias bound that is sharp for the MT functional and vanishes for remote outliers, and give a globally convergent linearized ADMM with closed-form updates.

title: Shaping the spectra of second harmonic laser by spatial focusing
abstract: Accurately controlling the spectral width of second harmonic generation (SHG) is critical in applications such as nonlinear microscopy, ultrafast spectroscopy, and quantum optics, where tailored spectral properties are required. Although it is known that the focal length of the lens used to focus the pump beam influences the SHG spectrum, a simple and precise theoretical understanding of this effect has been lacking. Here, we develop a theoretical model to describe how pump focusing conditions affect SHG spectral broadening, and experimentally validate the model using BBO crystals with lenses of 50 mm and 200 mm focal lengths. Our results establish a practical method for engineering the SHG spectral width through pump focusing, providing valuable guidance for designing nonlinear optical systems with specific spectral requirements.

title: Exploration via Activation-Space Steering for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains a language model by sampling responses, scoring them with an automatic verifier, and updating the policy from the resulting rewards. The policy therefore receives direct learning signals only from trajectories that appear in its rollouts. Yet repeated sampling from the same policy can concentrate on similar reasoning paths, leaving useful alternatives unexplored under a fixed rollout budget. We introduce Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), an online method for diversifying training rollouts. By clustering activation differences between correct and incorrect responses to the same problem, ASE builds a structured bank of latent exploration vectors. Different vectors are then applied to subsequent rollouts to explore alternative reasoning paths. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base trained on DAPO-Math-17k, ASE improves average Mean@8 across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks over GRPO by 4.87 and 1.87 percentage points, respectively, under the same rollout budget.

title: Decomposed Relation Extraction from Aviation Accident Narratives: Evaluating Transformer-Based Safety Knowledge Discovery under Relational Sparsity
abstract: Relation extraction from aviation accident narratives is challenging because genuine safety relations are sparse among possible concept pairs. This study evaluates a decomposed framework separating relation classification from concept identification. A benchmark of 300 National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) narratives containing 2,524 unique concept-text nodes was expanded into 21,038 ordered candidate pairs, with only 248 (1.18%) representing RESULTS_IN or CONTRIBUTES_TO relations. A TF-IDF Linear Support Vector Machine (SVM) and weighted RoBERTa classifier were developed using an independent graph-annotated resource with hard-negative sampling and frozen before sealed evaluation. Development Macro-F1 scores of 0.4738 (SVM) and 0.4809 (RoBERTa) declined to 0.2741 and 0.2420 under exhaustive evaluation, with Matthews correlation coefficients of 0.0128 and 0.0197. False positives dominated: the SVM recovered 96 reference relations but generated 7,018 false positives, while RoBERTa recovered 125 but generated 9,824. Post-test diagnostics revealed overlapping RoBERTa confidence distributions and false positives even within valid relation-category directions. Complementary end-to-end SmolLM2 evaluation identified missed and unsupported relations alongside malformed outputs. These findings demonstrate that known concept endpoints do not guarantee reliable relation extraction and that sampled-negative development performance may poorly reflect exhaustive evaluation. Controlling false positives and managing candidate-space sparsity remain essential for aviation safety knowledge extraction.

title: Heat-current-induced nonreciprocal phonon damping
abstract: Time-reversal symmetry enforces equal equilibrium linewidths for time-reversed phonon modes at opposite wave vectors. Here we show that a steady heat current can produce nonreciprocal anharmonic damping even in centrosymmetric nonmagnetic crystals. The effect arises from nonequilibrium occupations of scattering partners, which change the statistical weights of time-reversed three-phonon channels while their squared matrix elements remain equal. Within the single-mode relaxation-time approximation, we derive a linewidth correction that is linear in the temperature gradient and odd under wave-vector reversal. The response depends on scattering-partner velocities and equilibrium lifetimes and retains signed channel weights absent from the equilibrium linewidth. First-principles calculations for centrosymmetric MgO and diamond yield nonzero, mode-dependent linewidth corrections at selected finite wave vectors, demonstrating the mechanism in both ionic and covalent crystals. Reversing the heat current at fixed local temperature exchanges the broadening and narrowing of paired modes. This current-reversible linewidth contrast provides a spectral signature of occupation feedback, with potential implications for nonlinear phonon transport.

title: $Λ_b \to Λ\ell^+\ell^-$ and $Λ_b \to Λ^{\ast} \ell^+\ell^-$ decays with polarized leptons
abstract: We present an analysis of lepton polarization observables in the rare flavor-changing neutral current decays $Λ_b \to Λ\ell^+\ell^-$ and $Λ_b \to Λ^*\ell^+\ell^-$. These decays are driven by the quark-level transition $b \to s\ell^+\ell^-$ and are sensitive to short-distance physics within and beyond the Standard Model. We work within an effective Hamiltonian framework and derive single lepton polarization asymmetries, double lepton polarization asymmetries, and polarized forward-backward asymmetries using the helicity method. The observables are expressed in terms of transversity amplitudes and evaluated using state-of-the-art lattice QCD form factors. We analyze the $q^2$ dependence of several observables for both the ground-state $Λ$ and the excited $Λ^*(1520)$ final states and discuss sensitivities of the observables to chiral structure of the effective operators and complex Wilson coefficients.

title: On the Motivic K-Theories of Classifying Spaces of Cyclic 2-Groups
abstract: We compute the $2$-completed integral motivic homology, effective algebraic $K$-theory, and very effective Hermitian $K$-theory of the geometric classifying spaces $Bμ_{2^n}$, $n\geq 2$, over algebraically closed and real closed fields. We first carry out the corresponding classical calculations and, then obtain the motivic results using motivic spectral sequences and comparison techniques. The results reveal the classical $2$-torsion together with motivic $τ$-periodicity and $ρ$-torsion.

title: Data-driven accelerated multigrid method for Riesz space fractional diffusion equations
abstract: The multigrid method is one of the most efficient iterative methods for solving large structured linear systems, and its efficiency stems from the complementarity between the smoother and the coarse grid correction. In this paper, we consider the block Toeplitz linear system obtained by discretizing time dependent Riesz space fractional diffusion equations, and employ the weighted Jacobi iterative method as a smoother. The weighted Jacobi smoother features a simple structure and low computational cost, yet its smoothing property is highly dependent on the relaxation parameter. We adopt Gaussian process regression to select the relaxation parameter to accelerate the convergence of the multigrid method. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical analysis, which simultaneously verifies the effectiveness and superiority of the data-driven parameter selection strategy.

title: Long-wave Infrared Polarimetric Remote Sensing Image Fusion for Vehicle Detection
abstract: Blurred vehicle contours and low contrast limit detection performance in infrared remote sensing imagery, while existing fusion methods may introduce polarization noise and fail to integrate complementary information effectively. To address these limitations, we propose a Mamba-based infrared polarimetric remote sensing image fusion model. Infrared polarization information reflects surface material properties and geometry, providing complementary information to infrared intensity. The proposed method first combines long-wave infrared total intensity S0 and the degree of linear polarization (DoLP), using a physics-inspired polarization-response proxy and spatial structural continuity to extract guidance features. It then employs bidirectional state space scanning along horizontal, vertical, and both diagonal orientations to enable cross-modal feature fusion across the entire image. Prior-guided multi-window structural similarity, reconstruction constraints, and a relative lower-bound loss for polarization saliency are jointly introduced to suppress noise while preserving global background structures and target polarization features. In addition, we construct AIR-LWIR-Pol, a dataset of 1,901 accurately registered image pairs acquired using an airborne division-of-aperture long-wave infrared polarimetric imaging system, and evaluate downstream vehicle detection using YOLO11. The experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the comparison methods on four fusion metrics, including entropy and structural similarity. Vehicle detection mAP50 and mAP50-95 reach 55.0% and 29.4%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining physical priors with state space modeling for long-wave infrared polarization image fusion and support its use for target detection in complex remote sensing scenes.

title: MultiCard: Multiple Attribute Cardinality Estimation via Deep Learning
abstract: Cardinality estimation is essential for query optimization, but most existing learned estimators focus on a single predicate type, such as string LIKE clauses or numerical range filters. In practice, analytical workloads often combine both types, while the accuracy of string estimators tends to decrease with longer patterns. We introduce MultiCard, a comprehensive learned cardinality estimator that unifies LIKE predicates and numerical filters within a single end-to-end architecture. By combining a Transformer for long-range sparse patterns with an LSTM for short, frequent patterns, MultiCard achieves robust pattern modeling. In parallel, a numerical encoder integrates catalog histograms and structural predicate features, enabling the model to dynamically assess histogram estimation accuracy across different operators and data skew conditions. A final Transformer layer captures interactions among heterogeneous predicates before a multilayer perceptron predicts query cardinalities. We also introduce UPCI, a workload generator that produces length-balanced LIKE patterns, multi-column numerical predicates, and exact cardinality labels for training and evaluation. Experiments on five real-world datasets show that, for string-only workloads, MultiCard achieves the best or near-best Q-error across all datasets compared with state-of-the-art methods.
