The resulting convex legalization formulation satisfies the area, shape, separation, connectivity, and outline constraints while minimizing either the chip area or the displacement from the global floorplanning solution. Experiments on the GSRC, MCNC, and ICCAD 2023 contest benchmarks demonstrate that RPolyPlan reduces HPWL over the evaluated state-of-the-art methods by 7% and 6% in fixed-outline and outline-free experiments, respectively.

title: Diversity, Efficiency, and Incentives in Political Prediction Markets
abstract: Critics of political prediction markets argue that prices are biased because traders are not representative of voters. We test this claim by analyzing data from political betting markets spanning more than 100 years. Our analysis yields two main findings: (1) Acros markets, traders were not representative of the voters. (2) Prices were not biased by political preferences of participants. For the 2024 election, we analyzed anonymized data from Kalshi, a CFTC-regulated exchange, the largest regulated political prediction market in the U.S. Kalshi's traders were 86% male and half were under 30. In its first month of listing election contracts, Kalshi's prices were more accurate than every poll-based forecast in the national race, the seven battleground states, and nineteen Senate races, and no poll-based forecast would have been profitable to trade against them in any group of presidential contests. Its volume came from areas that voted 28% Republican, while 60% of volume went to Republican positions. Traders with a single trade placed 73% of their volume on Harris. The association between a trader's location and the direction of positions declines with trading activity and is zero among active traders, who account for most of the volume. Prices can be accurate with unrepresentative traders when the forecasts of profit-motivated traders do not depend on their demographics. Two other markets corroborate our findings. In New York's 1900 market, bettors were older than the population and drawn from finance. On PredictIt in 2016, which limited each trader to $850 per contract, positions followed registered party more closely, as our theory predicts when market restrictions do not allow profit-motivated traders to set the price. Prediction market efficiency is driven by financial incentives over demographic representativeness.

title: Dynamics of two bosons with density-assisted tunnelling in a one-dimensional tilted lattice
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of two bosons in a tilted one-dimensional optical lattice with both standard and density-assisted tunnelling. The relative sign of the two tunnelling processes strongly affects the Bloch dynamics, leading to distinct reinforcing and competing regimes. We examine how the tunnelling processes generate correlations and find that, in the absence of onsite interactions, the early-time entanglement growth follows the same scaling with the density-assisted tunnelling amplitude. Finite onsite interaction changes this picture by breaking the symmetry between the reinforcing and competing regimes and enhancing the correlation differently in two regimes. This shows how the interplay between the two tunnelling mechanisms can change dyanmics and entanglement in a controlled few-body setting. Particularly, at equal tunnelling amplitudes, the doublon and singlon sectors decouple completely for arbitrary onsite interaction, lattice tilting, and initial state.

title: Gaussian Integral Operator between Fock Spaces
abstract: We study Gaussian integral operators \[(Tf)(z)=\frac1π\int_{\mathbb C} e^{αz^2+β\overline w^{\,2}+γz\overline w+ηz+δ\overline w} f(w)e^{-|w|^2}\,dA(w)\] acting between Fock spaces $\mathcal F^p$ and $\mathcal F^q$, where $0<p,q\leq\infty$. We give complete characterizations of their boundedness and compactness in terms of explicit conditions on the parameters of the Gaussian kernel. The proofs are based on a unified approach combining reproducing-kernel estimates, atomic decompositions, and sampling sequences, together with a reduction to diagonal operators on sequence spaces. We also study Schatten-class membership on $\mathcal F^2$ and compute the Hilbert--Schmidt norm explicitly.

title: GALA: Geometry-Aware Language Model for Controllable Object Arrangement
abstract: Reasoning about fine-grained placement constraints, such as support and containment, is essential for realistic 3D scene creation. It remains a significant challenge for existing methods that rely on simplified object representations like oriented bounding box (OBB), which are blind to the detailed geometry. To address this limitation, we introduce GALA, a geometry-aware language model with explicit point cloud perception for controllable object placement. Our model performs autoregressively by predicting the 6D pose of one target object at a time conditioned on the scene context and placement instruction. We utilize a two-stage training strategy: the first stage aligns geometric and textual modalities through pretraining tasks, and the second stage fine-tunes the model for placement. To facilitate this task, we also curate a multi-source scene dataset covering diverse room types and fine-grained furniture arrangements, which will be open-sourced for community benefit. Experiments on our benchmark show our model significantly outperforms baselines without explicit geometric reasoning. We further develop a multi-stage plan-place-verify agent pipeline that uses the model for text-driven scene generation. Project Page: https://xccelephant.github.io/paper/gala/

title: Forty Questions: Identifying a Language Model from One-Word Answers
abstract: A model behind an API can be identified from its one-word answers to everyday questions such as "Name a sound" or "Name a poet". A model's profile records how often it gives each answer to each question. We attribute new answers to the model most likely to have given them. On a panel of 94 models, 40 answers identify the exact model 92.5% of the time, against 1.1% by chance. Profiles built through OpenRouter identified all ten models served by DeepInfra under blinded labels. A system prompt lowers accuracy by 6 to 16 points. We applied the method to 96 endpoints of 13 open models on OpenRouter, and 92 identify as the model they claim. Of the other four, one matches the claimed model with reasoning turned off. One serves Gemma 4 under the name Llama 4 Maverick: it names itself Gemma 4, and it is billed Gemma 4's token counts on every message. Two remain unresolved. Billing records also show context added to first-party models. Grok 4.7 is billed 1,247 input tokens for a one-line question that costs GPT-4o only 12 tokens, and five models state the current date without being billed for it. The questions come from a public census of model defaults, and the method costs cents per endpoint.

title: ChartEvo: Self-Evolving Agent Harnesses for Long-Tail Chart Reasoning
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have substantially advanced chart understanding and reasoning, yet their performance remains highly uneven across chart types. While modern MLLMs perform well on common charts, their accuracy drops sharply on long-tail charts with diverse visual structures and reasoning requirements. Tool-augmented agents can improve complex chart reasoning by introducing specialized visual capabilities, but manually engineering strategies and tools for the heterogeneous and evolving long tail is difficult to scale. We introduce \textbf{ChartEvo}, a recursive self-improvement framework that enables chart agents to adapt to underperforming chart types through experience-driven harness-level self-improvement. ChartEvo jointly evolves reusable chart-specific Skills and executable Tools, while learning reusable local tool-call chains to compose evolved capabilities and control the inference overhead of tool-augmented reasoning. On long-tail charts from ChartBench and ChartX, ChartEvo improves accuracy over its base MLLM, Qwen3.7-Plus, by \textbf{45.6\%} and \textbf{32.5\%}, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of recursive self-improvement for long-tail chart adaptation.

title: Automation of amplitude-level QED resummation with ACRAIC
abstract: Precision electroweak predictions for future $e^+e^-$ colliders will require levels of precision unmatched in collider physics and the modelling of multiple-photon emissions, and the exponentiation of the associated logarithms needs to be carefully considered. The Yennie-Frautschi-Suura theorem subtracts the infrared singularities to all orders and exponentiates them, leaving infrared-finite remainders which can be calculated order-by-order. Coherent exponentiation performs this subtraction at the amplitude level, preserving the interference between emissions, but has so far been available only for fermion-pair production, with hand-coded amplitudes. We present ACRAIC, an automated, amplitude-level realization of this subtraction for general scattering processes in Sherpa. This method allows us to construct an $\mathcal{O}(α)$ and $\mathcal{O}(α^2)$ amplitude level subtraction scheme, in which the infrared-finite remainders are tree-level helicity amplitudes with partition-dependent propagator shifts, computed by the Berends--Giele recursion, and the one-loop electroweak virtual enters through a per-helicity factor from the loop provider. At $\mathcal{O}(α^2)$ two independent matchings agree on the size of the missing higher orders to $\sim10^{-3}$, and the estimated perturbative uncertainty shrinks by about an order of magnitude relative to $\mathcal{O}(α)$.

title: HRoPE: Homography Relative Positional Encoding
abstract: Geometric Relative Positional Encoding has become the primary mechanism for injecting spatial inductive biases into multi-view transformers. Existing designs condition attention on camera-level frustums or ray-marched depth, associating cross-view tokens through the sensor geometry. Such sensor-centric formulations, however, describe only where a token is observed from, leaving the rich surface geometry of the scene region depicted by the token. In this paper, we advocate a shift toward surface-aware positional encoding that explicitly grounds patch tokens in the geometry of physical surfaces. We introduce HRoPE, which represents the local geometry of each patch as a slanted 3D plane, following the slanted support-window assumption of classical multi-view stereo. We inject token-level, plane-induced homographies into attention as relative transformations. This equips the transformer with a geometric prior for rectifying perspective distortions and aligning patch features across viewpoints. Our encoding requires no ground-truth geometry: the plane parameters can be predicted end-to-end under a view-synthesis objective alone, or derived from foundation models. Extensive experiments on RealEstate10K, CO3Dv2, and DL3DV show that our best variant of HRoPE consistently outperforms the evaluated geometric positional encodings for novel view synthesis. Extensive ablations and analysis show the effectiveness of the proposed encoding. Please refer to our project page at: https://gaohchen.github.io/HRoPE

title: Conformal Koopman Certificates for Nonlinear Multi-Agent Consensus on Time-Evolving Graphs
abstract: Robot fleets must often agree on a shared value before they act, over wireless networks that change as the robots move. Their supervisor needs a deadline: the number of communication rounds after which the fleet has agreed with a stated probability. Today it comes from simulation plus a safety margin, with an open probability of being met. We certify it. Our method, conformal Koopman certification, rests on one observation: averaged over the random network changes, the expected behaviour of the fleet evolves linearly, for any nonlinearity of the agents. The decay rate of this linear evolution gives the shape of the deadline. One remaining constant is calibrated from 200 short test runs by conformal prediction, a statistical method that turns any predictor into a guarantee that holds with a user-chosen probability. The certified deadline holds for every agreement tolerance at once and for any error in the estimated rate. The same linear model predicts the value the fleet will agree on and certifies how much corruption of the exchanged messages the collective decision absorbs. For 60 simulated robots the certified deadline was met in all 500 test runs against a 90\% target and exceeded the slowest run by 16\%. The classical worst-case bound exceeds that run by more than 160 orders of magnitude, a linearised deadline is missed in up to 26\% of runs, and direct conformal calibration costs 80 times more simulation per tolerance.

title: Local Work, Global Progress: A Convergence Theory of AI Agent Collaboration
abstract: Teams of large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly applied to complex tasks, but their collaboration protocols are mostly designed empirically, without convergence guarantees. We formalize collaborative problem solving as block optimization: each agent improves one part of a shared solution, guided by its local objective plus a correction for how its changes affect the other parts. A coordinator checks every proposal against the global objective and merges proposals that do not interfere with each other. We prove linear convergence up to an error floor that vanishes when the corrections are exact. Interfering proposals can also be merged once their combination has been checked; the rate then depends on how well the proposals actually combine, not on worst-case interactions. With GPT-OSS-120B agents on robot routing, a three-agent team finds collision-free plans in every run, better than those of a single agent that controls all robots. On a larger routing task, a six-agent team completes its search about twice as fast as the single agent (in median). Merging the best checked combination of proposals, rather than only proposals that do not interfere, cuts the team's search time by about 30%. With constants measured on the runs, our convergence bound holds in every round and follows the observed progress. We also test the theory on query planning in SQLite and on a synthetic task.

title: Holographic Calculation of Semileptonic Form Factors and the Isgur--Wise Function for $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}$ Decays
abstract: We present a holographic analysis of the semileptonic decays $B \to D \ell \barν_\ell$ and $B_s \to D_s \ell \barν_\ell$ within the Softwall Model (SWM) and the Non-Quadratic Softwall Model (NQSWM). We extract the Isgur-Wise function from the overlap integral of bulk wavefunctions, with model parameters fixed by the heavy-light meson spectra. We impose Heavy Quark Symmetry (HQS) at zero recoil and address the apparent paradox of a non-conserved electroweak current dual to a massless bulk vector field. We argue that the non-conservation, arising from explicit flavor-- symmetry breaking by quark masses, does not generate an anomalous dimension. Hence the bulk field remains massless, and the non-conservation is \emph{encoded} in the independent boundary couplings $g_+$ and $g_-$. Our predictions for the branching fractions are in good agreement with LHCb data for $B_s \to D_s$ decays. The lepton-flavor universality ratios $R(D)$ and $R(D_s)$ are consistent with Standard Model and lattice QCD predictions. We find that the holographic models reproduce the universality of the Isgur-Wise function near zero recoil, while discrepancies at maximum recoil suggest that a more complete treatment of higher-order $1/m_Q$ corrections is needed.

title: Improved automatic speech-based cognitive assessment using neuropsychologically calibrated diagnostic labels
abstract: Although automatic detection of cognitive impairment from conversational speech is a promising way, it becomes less accurate, as large real-world datasets often contain unreliable diagnostic labels due to self-referral and limited clinical verification, and here we investigated whether neuropsychologically calibrated diagnostic relabeling improves it. We analysed 138 hours of conversational speech from 720 participants, recalibrating unreliable diagnostic labels using attention, executive function, and memory performance via external clinical thresholds, Gaussian, and normative z-score calibration. Transformer-based classifiers were trained using both original and recalibrated labels and evaluated internally on 150 clinically verified participants and externally on Pitt, ADReSS and PROCESS-2 datasets. Memory- and MoCA-based z-score calibration produced the greatest improvements. Using our internal dataset, $F_1$ increased from $0.70$ to $0.83$ ($+13\%$) and from $0.54$ to $0.66$ ($+12\%$) for binary and multiclass classification, respectively. For external validation, the increases are $+4\%$, $+5\%$ and $+9\%$ on Pitt, ADReSS and PROCESS-2 corpus. Neuropsychologically calibrated relabeling substantially improves speech-based cognitive assessment, highlighting label quality, rather than model architecture, as a critical bottleneck in clinical AI for dementia screening.

title: CPVB-RG: Cross-Prior Visual Bridging for Prior-Aware Chest X-Ray Report Generation
abstract: Radiologists interpret follow-up chest X-rays by comparing current and prior examinations to identify new, resolved or progressing findings. Most report generation systems either omit this longitudinal context or fuse prior features without distinguishing interval changes from anatomy that remains stable over time. We propose CPVB-RG, a prior-aware framework that combines current and prior radiographs with available clinical text. Its Cross-Prior Visual Bridge (CPVB) contains Progression-Guided Focus Attention (PGFA) and two Cross-Attention units. PGFA is designed to contrast progression-difference attention with shared-spatial attention, aiming to reduce invariant responses whilst retaining coarse spatial correspondence between examinations. The Cross-Attention units then connect the resulting longitudinal visual evidence with clinical semantics. CPVB-RG is trained in two stages, using prior-guided image-text alignment followed by autoregressive report generation with a lightweight language decoder. Experiments on MIMIC-CXR and IU X-Ray show consistent improvements across language and clinical metrics. On MIMIC-CXR, CPVB-RG achieves 0.2847 F1RadGraph and 0.6692 VLScore, with statistically significant gains over the closest decoder-matched prior-aware baseline. These results support the effectiveness of the proposed difference-aware and spatially guided fusion design for prior-aware chest X-ray report generation.

title: Distributed Platoon Control for Safe and Smooth Crossing at an Unsignalized Intersection-Part I: Stability Analysis
abstract: We propose a distributed platoon controller that guarantees safe and smooth crossing of multi-vehicle systems at an unsignalized intersection. To support the stability analysis, we consider a multi-vehicle platoon maneuvering along a closed path with a single unsignalized intersection. Unlike traditional bi-level decoupled designs on open paths, which primarily focus on intersection control while neglecting its coupling with platoon convergence, and thus hindering rigorous convergence analysis, the closed-path setting allows us to analyze the asymptotic behavior of the platoon. The local exponential convergence analysis of the switched closed-loop system, induced by repeated vehicle switching at the intersection, is presented. Under some mild conditions on the controller gains, we show that safe intersection crossing is ensured during the transient phase and smooth crossing is achieved in steady state, where all vehicles travel at a common constant speed while avoiding collisions at the intersection. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed distributed controller is demonstrated in a high-fidelity CARLA simulator using multiple commercial vehicle models.

title: AGGR-Mamba: Mamba-based Network with Attention-Guided Gated Residual Refinement for Undersampled MRI Reconstruction
abstract: Undersampled magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction aims to recover high-quality images from partially acquired k-space data, thereby reducing scan time. However, missing frequency-domain measurements often lead to residual aliasing artifacts, blurred edges, and loss of local structural details. In this paper, we propose AGGR-Mamba, a lightweight output-stage residual refinement method built upon a Mamba backbone for undersampled brain MRI reconstruction. The Mamba backbone first produces an initial reconstruction, and the proposed refinement modules then correct the remaining local errors and high-frequency artifacts in a controlled residual manner. Specifically, an Attention Refine Head is introduced to recalibrate local anatomical structures, edge textures, and residual-error regions through channel and spatial attention. In addition, a GDFN-style gated residual refinement branch is designed to selectively preserve informative residual features while suppressing redundant or unstable responses. By combining attention-based recalibration with gated residual selection, AGGR-Mamba improves local structure recovery without substantially disturbing the backbone reconstruction. Experiments are conducted on the IXI brain MRI dataset with T1- and T2-weighted images under acceleration factors of R=4 and R=8. The results show that AGGR-Mamba achieves competitive PSNR and SSIM performance across different reconstruction settings, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed output-stage refinement strategy.

title: Real-Time 24-hour Ahead Forecasting of Solar Energetic Particle Events with SEPNET-PRISM-R
abstract: Solar energetic particle (SEP) events, operationally defined as proton flux exceeding 10 pfu in the >10 MeV channel, threaten spacecraft systems, astronaut safety, and high latitude aviation, yet continuous real-time forecasting with adequate lead time remains difficult. We present SEPNET-PRISM-R, a near-real-time system that issues hourly, 24 hour ahead probabilistic SEP forecasts. The model integrates multimodal solar data - including active region patches, flare features, coronal mass ejection (CME) characteristics, and historical proton flux - to concurrently predict SEP occurrences, peak proton flux, soft X-ray flux, and CME velocity, with the primary objective being SEP forecasting. Building on existing literature, SEPNET-PRISM-R enhances operational performance by incorporating a postprocessing module that enables cross-validated decision making and interpretable quantification of feature importance. The training dataset spans from February 1986 to September 2025, with subsequent forecasts generated sequentially through the present via a real-time space weather prediction platform that provides predictive probabilities, feature attributions, and historical analogs, enabling more reliable and informed operational decision-making. The proposed framework substantially suppresses false alarm rates while maintaining robust event detection capabilities, as evidenced by case studies and aggregate statistics.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Distributed Radio Map Estimation in Decentralized Wireless Networks
abstract: Federated learning based radio map estimation (RME) approaches rely on frequent exchange of high-dimensional model updates and often require a central server for collaboration coordination and update aggregation. This incurs prohibitively high communication overhead, rendering them impractical for bandwidth-constrained mobile and wireless edge networks. Moreover, in practical mobile sensing scenarios, sparse and unevenly collected measurements lead to estimation uncertainty, which is critical for guiding RME and collaboration among distributed nodes. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an uncertainty-aware distributed radio map estimation (UA-D-RME) framework for decentralized networks. In UA-D-RME, each node locally infers a probabilistic model from its sparse measurements to estimate both its local radio map and the associated estimation uncertainty. Instead of exchanging raw data or model updates, neighboring nodes communicate only low-dimensional statistical information, including radio map and uncertainty measures over their overlapping monitoring areas. An uncertainty-aware statistical consensus mechanism is then developed to iteratively align probabilistic models in neighborhood by ensuring consistency on estimation confidence. Theoretical analysis establishes the convergence of the proposed consensus mechanism and characterizes the distributed generalization performance of the proposed UA-D-RME method. Experiments on urban radio map datasets verify that UA-D-RME achieves desired reconstruction accuracy comparable to the centralized RME benchmark while reducing communication costs and without exchanging raw measurements.

title: Adaptive Replay Refinement: Allocating Test-Time Compute Between Revision and Resampling
abstract: Test-time scaling allocates additional inference compute to refining existing solutions or generating new ones. This raises a fundamental question: Should I keep improving this solution, or stop working on it and try a completely new solution? Existing methods make this decision using fixed refinement schedules, self-verification judgments, or learned controllers, which can waste compute or rely on signals that may be incorrect or require additional training. We introduce Adaptive Replay Refinement (ARR), a training-free method that detects when a stationary revision reaches a fixed point and reallocates the released compute to a new independent sample; replay decoding treats the current solution as a draft and verifies unchanged tokens in parallel, enabling efficient fixed-point detection. Across seven models from five families and seven benchmarks, ARR matches majority voting on three of five mathematical reasoning benchmarks at equal compute, while reducing critical-path serial passes by up to 2.4 times. On MATH500, ARR achieves 84.6% accuracy with only 41% of the serial passes required by majority voting. These results demonstrate that detecting refinement exhaustion enables adaptive reallocation from revision to independent sampling, improving inference efficiency while highlighting the limits of self-revision. Code is available at https://github.com/AhsanBilal7/adaptive_refine.

title: Random $C^*$-subalgebras
abstract: Given a discrete countable group $Γ$, we introduce the concept of random subalgebras of the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(Γ)$. This extends the existing theory of invariant random subgroups and the one of invariant random subalgebras of the group von Neumann algebra ${\rm L}(Γ)$. As applications, we provide a characterisation of $C^*$-simplicity, a condition for amenability of the group and show the existence and uniqueness of a maximal nuclear $Γ$-invariant unital $C^*$-subalgebra of $C^*_r(Γ)$. Moreover, we give a topological characterisation of exactness of any separable unital $C^*$-algebra. Finally, we study exotic random subalgebras of $C^*_r(Γ)$ and super-exotic random subalgebras of ${\rm L}(Γ)$, that is, random subalgebras which do not arise purely from random subgroups of $Γ$ and not from random subalgebras of $C^*_r(Γ)$, respectively.

title: Open Science with the LHCb Ntupling Service
abstract: The data samples collected at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN are highly valuable, and the analysis of these data has led to numerous discoveries and the 2025 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics. Preserving and providing open access to these data for future analysts is imperative to maximize the scientific output of the collected data. The LHCb collaboration has developed a novel approach to this pursuit of open science, the LHCb Ntupling Service: a web service for on-demand production and publishing of custom LHCb open data, providing open access to both Run 1, and for the first time, Run 2 proton-proton collision data collected by the LHCb experiment, amounting to over 4 PB of data to explore.

title: Twisted group codes of dimension 2 and 3
abstract: It is known that all group codes of dimension at most $3$ are permutation equivalent to abelian group codes. We prove that twisted group codes of dimension at most $3$ are monomially equivalent either to an abelian group code or to an irreducible constacyclic code, and in the second case we describe the code explicitly by means of a trace map. Monomial equivalence cannot be replaced by permutation equivalence, and the second case cannot be avoided: the ternary tetracode is an ideal of $\mathbb F_3[x]/(x^4+1)$ but it is not monomially equivalent to any group code. More generally, we give two infinite families, in dimensions $2$ and $3$, of irreducible constacyclic codes which attain the Griesmer bound, whereas every group code with the same length and dimension has smaller minimum distance.

title: Classical spin liquids in the kagome Ising model, and their link with magnetoelasticity
abstract: We investigate a nearest-neighbor Ising model on the kagome lattice coupled to elastic lattice distortions. By integrating out the lattice degrees of freedom, we derive an approximate spin-only description in terms of a kagome \(J_1\)-\(J_2\)-\(J_{3}\) Ising model with interactions extending to third nearest-neighbors. Using tensor network methods complemented by classical Monte Carlo simulations, we revisit its zero-temperature phase diagram and characterize the ground states studied more than thirty years ago. We discover three phases with extensive zero-temperature entropy and algebraically decaying spin correlations. Importantly, these states are not confined to fine-tuned points or frontiers between phases, but occupy extended areas of parameter space. Their quasi long-range order is reflected in Bragg-like peaks in the structure factors; we relate this, and other properties, to diverse phases found in Ising and Heisenberg models. Finally, we trace the trajectories generated by the magnetoelastic coupling through the effective-model phase diagram, explaining the emergence of self-frustration for the unfrustrated magnetoelastic model with ferromagnetic interactions.

title: Ordered Trees with Linear Off-Diagonal Ramsey Numbers
abstract: We characterize the following three classes of ordered trees: $\qquad$ (1) trees $T$ satisfying $R_<(T,K_n)=O(n)$; $\qquad$ (2) $χ$-bounding trees; $\qquad$ (3) Ramsey-good trees. In particular, we show that the first two classes coincide. The second characterization answers a question of Axenovich, Rollin and Ueckerdt, and the third resolves a problem of Balko and Poljak. In our proof, we also introduce several novel constructions of ordered graphs with sublinear independence number, giving lower bounds on $R_<(F,K_n)$ for various ordered forests $F$.

title: Primal-Dual Adaptive Subgradient Methods
abstract: We propose adaptive primal-dual subgradient methods for constrained convex optimization. Our first method applies an AdaGrad-style step-sizes to the dual problem and recovers primal solutions by averaging the associated Fenchel-type oracle outputs. It achieves $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2})$ convergence for the dual objective residual, primal objective residual, and feasibility gap in the nonsmooth regime, while automatically improving to $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$ when the dual objective is smooth. We further develop an accelerated variant, which retains the $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2})$ nonsmooth rate while achieving $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ convergence in the smooth regime under mild assumptions. These guarantees require no prior knowledge of the underlying regularity. We demonstrate the empirical performance of the proposed methods on optimal transport and semidefinite relaxation of the Max-Cut problem.

title: Gaussian Fluctuations of the Gradient of the Fréchet Function and Nonstandard Asymptotics of Sample Fréchet Means
abstract: We establish a central limit theorem for the gradient of the population Fréchet function in local Euclidean coordinates on a metric space. Assuming a unique population mean, a consistent measurable sequence of sample means, semiconcavity and moment bounds for the squared distance functions, and local $C^{1,α}$ regularity of the population Fréchet function, we prove an asymptotic linear representation for the gradient of the population Fréchet function evaluated at the sample mean. The leading term is the negative empirical average of the gradients of the squared distance functions at the population mean; these gradients exist almost surely under our assumptions. On connected complete Riemannian manifolds, uniqueness of the population mean, existence of a $(2+η)$-moment, and local $C^{1,α}$ regularity suffice, and the leading term is expressed through the logarithm map. To control the empirical process uniformly over a neighborhood where squared distance functions may be nonsmooth, we use one-sided partial derivatives of the squared distance functions. The key estimate is a polynomial bound on the $L^2$ bracketing numbers of the resulting function classes. We also give a sufficient condition for the regularity of the population Fréchet function through probability bounds for neighborhoods of cut loci. We then show how the local behavior of the population Fréchet function transforms these Gaussian fluctuations into limit distributions for suitably rescaled sample Fréchet means, allowing for anisotropic scaling and non-Gaussian limits. Polynomial, logarithmic, and oscillatory examples illustrate the applicability and limitations of this approach.

title: Learning Normal Coordinates on Riemannian Manifolds with Flow Charts
abstract: Riemannian manifolds are powerful models for problems with non-Euclidean structure. Recent work in geometric machine learning has focused on training deep neural networks to learn Riemannian metrics from high-dimensional data. However, many geometric algorithms require repeated evaluations of the exponential and logarithmic maps, whose high computational cost restricts the utility of learned Riemannian manifolds in practice. We propose to address this cost by training a conditional invertible neural network, called a flow chart, to approximate normal coordinates around points on a given Riemannian manifold. With this approach, the exponential and logarithmic maps can be approximated by fast Euclidean operations in the model's learned coordinate space. Our main contribution is an efficient loss function for training flow charts that is nonnegative and, under suitable domain assumptions, is zero precisely when the chart is normal. Across sixteen synthetic and data-derived geometries, flow charts are competitive with a specialized neural geodesic interpolator for logarithmic map estimation, while also being able to estimate the exponential map. When pretrained, flow charts provide a median speedup of 60-70x over numerical baselines at comparable logarithmic map estimation error, and their learned coordinates improve the accuracy of a numerical geodesic solver.

title: Reward Misspecification Degrades Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
abstract: Monitoring the chain-of-thought (CoT) of language models (LMs) is a key strategy for detecting and preventing misbehaviors for AI safety. As such, it is critical to identify reinforcement learning (RL) practices that lead to unmonitorable chain-of-thought. One such practice may be unavoidable: reward misspecification. As RL environments become more complex, it is infeasible to have perfect verification, and models are rewarded for behaviors that are different from the true task intent. We show that reward misspecification alone already degrades monitorability. We create a testbed with pairs of true reward aligned with task intent and misspecified rewards that favor a different behavior, so that reward hacking can be induced by training and labeled verifiably. Across three models and three tasks, CoT monitorability remains low as models' hack rates increase: the CoTs keep reasoning about the task intent while the outputs violate the intent and get rewarded. To mitigate unmonitorability without prior knowledge of the true reward or the hack, we collect rollouts with diverse rewards across training steps and use a LM to infer a reward description. We then inject the description into the input, which teaches the model to verbalize the reward. This reward description training improves monitorability by an average of 24% or 42% absolute, depending on the metric, across all models and tasks, and yields CoTs that reason about the misspecified reward explicitly. Code is available at https://github.com/Lorenayannnnn/reward-misspecification-degrades-cot-monitorability.

title: Steady-state cooperative emission of interlayer excitons in atomically thin light-emitting diodes
abstract: When an ensemble of emitters is confined within an optical wavelength, its radiation can become correlated, leading to cooperative emission. In two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) electron-hole bilayers, strong light-matter coupling enables the formation of interlayer excitons (IXs), long-lived dipolar excitations that provide an ideal setting for emergent collective phenomena. Here, we engineer an atomically thin light-emitting diode (LED) that generates electroluminescence (EL) from electrically injected IXs that are confined near the sample edges by an edge-enhanced fringing electric field. By measuring Hanbury-Brown-Twiss photon-photon correlations, we find pronounced signatures of collective decay in the form of large photon bunching followed by finite delay antibunching and bunching revivals. These emitter correlation signatures disappear when free charge carriers are doped to form a degenerate Fermi sea but are enhanced by the introduction of localized electrons. The results are consistent with a many-body quantum master equation that models the steady-state superradiant photon statistics of incoherently injected IXs. Our work establishes steady-state cooperative emission in a 2D TMD LED as a platform for studying strong light-matter interactions in electrically driven, non-equilibrium phases of Bose-Fermi mixtures.

title: An Erdős-Szekeres-Type Result on Permutation Patterns
abstract: We construct an infinite set of patterns $(p,q)$ where $p$ is an almost increasing permutation and $q$ is an almost decreasing permutation, such that the exponential growth rate of permutations avoiding $(p,q)$ is 2. This extends a classical result of Erdős and Szekeres.

title: Nonequivalence of $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear and $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear generalized Hadamard codes for odd primes
abstract: The $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-additive codes are subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}_p^{α_1}\times\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}^{α_2}$, and they can be seen as linear codes over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ when $α_2=0$, as $\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-additive codes when $α_1=0$, and as $\mathbb{Z}_2\mathbb{Z}_4$-additive codes when $p=2$. A $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear generalized Hadamard (GH) code is a GH code over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ which is the Gray map image of a $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-additive code. For every prime $p$, there are recursive constructions of $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear GH codes $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ with $α_1\neq0$ and $α_2\neq0$, and of $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear GH codes $\bar H_p^{t_1,\dots,t_s}$. We show that the kernel blocks of a nonlinear code $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ give equivalent punctured codes, and that these punctured codes are linear. Any of them is called the derived code of $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$. We also determine the ranks of the codes $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ and $\bar H_p^{t_1,t_2}$. For odd $p$, the rank of $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ depends on the Bernoulli numbers modulo $p$. By comparing the derived codes and the ranks, we show that, for odd $p$, no code $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ is equivalent to any of these $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear GH codes. For $p=2$, a nonlinear code $H_2^{t_1,t_2}$ is equivalent to a $\mathbb{Z}_{2^s}$-linear Hadamard code if and only if $t_2\geq2$. Finally, we count the nonequivalent codes in the union of both families.

title: Space-time large deviations for continuum birth-and-death processes
abstract: We establish a space-time large deviation principle for the empirical process of spatial birth-and-death dynamics in the continuum with area interaction at arbitrary inverse temperature, including the free evolution. The good rate function is the dynamical specific relative entropy with respect to the dynamics, and the result holds on the space of space-time stationary laws on the Skorokhod path space, equipped with the topology of weak convergence. For the time marginals of the empirical process, we identify the rate function in terms of the Hellinger distance between the birth and the death measure of the observed point process, which vanishes exactly at the translation-invariant Gibbs point processes. This proves a continuum version of conjectures of Dai Pra and Handa, and connects space-time large deviations with entropy production.

title: Stability of 2D MHD with Only Horizontal Dissipation near a Background Magnetic Field on $\mathbb{R}^2$
abstract: Whether the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with dissipation in only one direction are stable in $H^2$ on the whole plane is a well-known open problem: without transverse dissipation, a cubic interaction fails to be time-integrable. We show that a magnetic field removes this obstruction. For the 2D incompressible MHD equations on $\mathbb R^2$ in which both the viscosity $ν$ and the magnetic diffusivity $μ$ act only in the horizontal direction, we prove the global nonlinear $H^2$ stability of every background field $γe_2$ aligned with the non-dissipative direction, with a stability threshold that is explicit in $ν$, $μ$ and $γ$. The stabilizing mechanism is genuinely nonlinear: at the linear level the background field produces no damping at all in the vertical direction. Instead, in Elsässer variables the obstruction becomes an interaction between Alfvén waves travelling in opposite directions, and we identify nonlinear dissipative quantities that measure the overlap of these waves and are time-integrable although neither wave decays. We then sharpen the threshold by a space--time div--curl estimate for balance laws in the $(t,x_2)$-plane. For $ν=μ\leq1\leqγ$, the admissible perturbations are of size $ν^{2/3}γ^{1/3}$, improving the direct scale $ν$ and growing without bound as the background field strengthens.

title: Generative Diffusion Models for Secure UAV-ISAC with Real-Time Target Tracking
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platforms with integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) are prime candidates for surveillance missions, in which a dual-function drone tracks a mobile target and alerts a ground station when the target enters a protected region. Such alerts generate event-triggered communication traffic. By observing the change in the traffic, an eavesdropper (Eve) can therefore learn in real time whether the target is detected inside the protected region without decoding any message. Existing physical-layer security techniques protect the message content or hide that a transmission occurs, but the composition of the traffic remains exposed. We formulate the threat as traffic-composition covertness and propose a keyless diffusion-based transmission scheme that hides the triggered traffic. The scheme superposes the beamformed information streams of the UAV with a message-agnostic safeguard waveform generated by a conditional denoising diffusion implicit model. Training shapes the safeguard distribution such that triggered and non-triggered slots become statistically indistinguishable at Eve. The legitimate user shares no secret key with the UAV. We formulate the joint design as a rate maximization under covertness, reliability, and sensing constraints, with the sensing accuracy measured by the posterior Cramér-Rao bound (PCRB) of the beam-dependent tracking problem. Our numerical results show that, with multiple transmit antennas and an Eve signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $5$~dB, a learned Eve stays near the blind guess of $0.5$ for every safeguard beam split, a detector that knows the safeguard model reaches $0.71$ to $0.73$ inside Bob's main lobe and $0.53$ to $0.55$ outside it, while the average position PCRB varies only between $0.59$ and $0.70$~m$^2$.

title: Recommending Bacterial Cultivation Conditions from 16S rRNA
abstract: Recommending bacterial cultivation conditions from sequence data is a challenging structured problem characterized by missing standardized benchmarks and limited use of sequence structure. To address this, we introduce DSNI, a benchmark of 65,023 bacterial strains with phylogeny-aware splits, pairing 16S rRNA sequences with four cultivation conditions (media, temperature, pH, oxygen). Exploiting the mosaic structure of 16S rRNA, where hypervariable regions support discrimination and conserved regions support primer design, we propose a Variability-Gated Encoder that learns position-dependent importance weights conditioned on biological features (region type, position, and local complexity). The gating module adds minimal overhead (1,280 parameters, <1%) while providing an explicit inductive bias valuable in low-data regimes. Experiments demonstrate that the learnable gate improves flat Transformers by 4.7% in joint accuracy and complements RNABERT, yielding 44.2% exact-match joint accuracy. The model also recovers 90.2% of ground-truth cultivation protocols within its top-25 recommendations, narrowing the exhaustive search space by approximately 60 times.

title: From Abstraction to Action: DSLs for Natural Language Abstraction Interpretation and Execution
abstract: Natural-language instructions often rely on high-level abstractions, such as asking an agent to ``stack blocks in a pyramid.'' Interpreting abstract instructions requires models to both identify the abstraction intended by the speaker, and unroll it into the many concrete actions that instantiate it. Language models struggle here: prior work has shown that performance degrades as the level of abstraction in the instruction rises. To bridge the gap between natural language abstraction and concrete actions, we propose to borrow from coding environments the notion of a {\em domain-specific language} (DSL), an explicit representation layer whose documented primitives name recurring abstractions that expand into concrete actions. We demonstrate the efficacy of DSLs for NL interpretation on \textsc{Hexagons}, a visually-grounded instruction-following task graded for abstraction. We further ask whether language models can induce such DSLs themselves from domain data. Our results show that while code generation consistently improves over direct inference, code generation over a human-curated DSL yields dramatic gains, up to 10 absolute F1 points, reaching the human skyline, with gains concentrated at {\em higher} abstraction levels. We confirm this pattern on the \textsc{Text2CAD} benchmark. At the same time, model-induced DSLs recover only part of this gain, remaining inconsistent across runs and short of their human-curated counterpart. Overall, the right representation closes much of the gap caused by high abstraction --- but inducing that layer of representation automatically is where models still fall short, and where we see a strong opportunity for the community to make progress.

title: A terminal-group and fluorination matrix for designing polar nematic liquid crystals
abstract: Lateral fluorination has emerged as a powerful design variable in the design of polar liquid crystals, but its interplay with terminal-group identity remains poorly understood. Here we report a 40-member matrix of biphenyl-ester-phenyl mesogens that independently varies lateral core fluorination and terminal-group identity. Increasing lateral fluorination generally suppresses apolar mesophases and clearing points, however this same change can enable polar nematic phase behaviour in conjunction with suitable terminal units. Graph Fourier analysis of conformer averaged atomic charges shows polar materials occupy a high-frequency region of charge-spectral space, consistent with a bond-scale electrostatic motif. Different terminal units can bias this towards higher or lower frequencies, and in doing so can enable polar order to emerge.

title: Towards Consistent Geospatial Representations: Aligning One Encoder to Many Foundation Models
abstract: Geospatial foundation models (GFMs) differ widely in pretraining objective, modality and resolution, and none leads across benchmarks. We ask whether their representations are complementary, and whether a single encoder can inherit that complementarity. We introduce Pangaea-Latents, an extension of the Pangaea benchmark providing frozen embeddings of $5$ GFMs over its $11$ datasets, along with reproduced baselines, and find GFM embeddings to be neither redundant nor disjoint. We then propose GeoMixture, a preliminary framework to align a ViT to several GFMs per dataset through a multi-representation alignment (mREPA) objective. Our encoder ties the best GFM in average rank across nine Pangaea datasets, trading peak performance for cross-task consistency.

title: Debiased Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Amortized Bayesian Semi-Parametric Inference
abstract: Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) have recently gained popularity as an end-to-end approach to amortized Bayesian inference. Yet, their statistical behavior for semi-parametric targets, such as means under missingness or causal effects, remains poorly understood. In this work, we develop theoretical foundations for debiased PFNs to perform inference on finite-dimensional targets in general semi-parametric settings. First, we show that, despite being Bayes-optimal with respect to the target, an idealized PFN can exhibit a posterior concentration rate that implicitly depends on the concentration rates of (latent) nuisance functions and can become slower as the prior becomes more diverse. Then, to speed up the target posterior concentration rates, we introduce two generic debiasing strategies based on efficient influence functions: (i) a label correction and (ii) a prior correction. Finally, we show that the debiased PFNs (i) & (ii) possess concentration rates that asymptotically match a convergence rate given by traditional frequentist bias-corrected estimators. In this way, we establish a novel connection between amortized Bayesian inference with PFNs and frequentist semi-parametric efficiency theory. Under additional assumptions, this allows us to guarantee local and global optimality of PFN-based estimators (namely, the Bernstein-von Mises property and minimax optimality, respectively). Therefore, our work provides guidelines for designing debiased PFNs for semi-parametric inference with principled and provable asymptotic guarantees.

title: Disclosure Begets Disclosure: A Self-Reinforcing Privacy Loop in LLM Agents with Persistent Memory
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use persistent memory to personalize responses, and personal attributes in this memory pose a privacy risk if exposed. We ask how consulting memory during dialogue changes what users go on to say, and thus what the memory comes to reveal. In multi-session simulations, a simulated user with 24 personal attributes talks with a support agent that does or does not consult memory, and in both settings attributes are inferred from the full accumulated record. Across four support models, memory raises response quality but also empirical leakage, the share of attribute values correctly inferred from the record, by a margin that widens over sessions. The cause is a loop in ordinary, non-adversarial assistance. Memory-conditioned responses carry earlier values forward, often as presuppositions, and users affirm them or leave them uncorrected, so that cues and the agent's own guesses become recorded values. The loop reinforces itself, and removing the agent's mentions of an attribute lowers its later disclosure about twice as much as single-turn effects predict. Users cannot leave it on their own, since correcting a value discloses the attribute, declining to discuss it shifts later predictions toward sensitive values, and incorrect values left in place become entrenched. The loop is best weakened at the agent's response. Instructing the agent not to state or presuppose attributes brings leakage to about the no-memory level while keeping most of the quality gains, whereas filtering or anonymizing what users say or what is stored gives up much of them.

title: ABACUS: A Benchmark for Image Editing Models to Assess Object Category and Counting Under Scene Conservation
abstract: Instruction-based image editing models can now add, remove a specified number of objects or change their category while preserving the scene. Yet these models often fail to produce the correct number, and these failures grow sharply as scenes become more complex and the requested count increases. Current benchmarks largely miss this problem: they score edits with holistic similarity metrics or with vision-language model (VLM) judges that are themselves poor at counting, so numerical errors go unnoticed or are graded incorrectly. As a result, the true numerical ability of today's editing models has never been accurately measured. We address this issue with ABACUS, a new benchmark, evaluation protocol and dedicated scoring metric for numerical image editing. Our protocol is judge-free: no VLM or MLLM scores an edit or counts objects (a VLM only confirms the category of rare ambiguous crops). Instead, it verifies each edit at the instance level against panoptic ground truth confirmed by detector consensus, checking both that the exact requested count was achieved and that the rest of the scene was preserved, across the add, remove and change operations. By evaluating leading image editors, our method reveals substantial numerical editing failures that worsen with increasing scene complexity and object count; failures that prior benchmarks often overlooked or misjudged.

title: Area gaps for minimal surfaces in spheres
abstract: In this paper, we prove that a linearly full minimal $2$-torus in $\mathbb{S}^N$ with $N\geq 5$ must have area $>2π^2$, and that a linearly full closed minimal surface in $\mathbb{S}^N$ with $N\geq 9$ must have area $>8π$. These results verify the Willmore conjecture and the generalized Willmore conjecture in higher codimension for minimal surfaces. The area gaps are obtained by applying the Cheng--Li--Yau comparison theorem and deriving a lower bound of the heat trace, where the monotonicity of the shifted normalized Riesz mean is used. We also establish a volume gap above the balanced Clifford product for linearly full closed minimal $n$-submanifolds in $\mathbb{S}^N$ when $n=3$, $N\geq 9$, or $n\geq 4$, $N\geq 3n-1$.

title: Stabilizing Filters for Graph Signal Generation
abstract: Generating graph signals is an important task in machine learning, and incorporating the underlying graph into a generative model enables structurally-informed distribution modeling. However, said graph is often noisy or imperfectly estimated, and structural errors can affect the generative process and the resulting signal distribution. While recent work has established stability guarantees for graph neural ordinary differential equations, the robustness of graph-aware reference dynamics, as used in topological Schrödinger bridge models, remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the structural stability of continuous-time generative models whose dynamics combine a graph filter with a learned graph neural network. We first derive a Wasserstein stability bound that quantifies the effect of graph perturbations on the generated signal distributions. Informed by this analysis, we then propose a principled framework for designing graph filters that balance structural stability with induced signal smoothing. We characterize the optimal filter design and provide an explicit family of polynomial filters with provable stability guarantees. Experiments on synthetic graphs and real-world fMRI signals support our theoretical findings, illustrating the enhanced structural stability of the proposed filters while preserving generative performance.

title: Causality violation in the holographic approach to N=4 SYM theory at finite 't Hooft coupling
abstract: In the AdS/CFT correspondence, correlation functions of the energy-momentum tensor in N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory at large but finite 't Hooft coupling can be studied using higher-derivative corrections to supergravity. We show that the commonly used holographic prescription for correlation functions which is obtained by truncating the equations of motion at order $(α')^3$ implies that the thermal equilibrium state of N=4 SYM theory in the planar limit is dynamically unstable at arbitrarily large finite 't Hooft coupling. The instability is a reflection of the unphysical causality violation brought about by treating perturbatively-derived equations as if they were non-perturbative, analogous to the instability of AdS black branes in five-dimensional Gauss-Bonnet gravity. While other holographic prescriptions for treating the $O(α'^3)$ corrections to supergravity may alleviate the pathology introduced by the truncation, the validity regime of the results obtained by any prescription at $O(α'^3)$ must be limited to the strict perturbative treatment of the $O(α'^3)$ effects on N=4 SYM observables.

title: Spherical harmonics and infinitesimal projective transformations
abstract: Consider the space of $C^\infty$-functions on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ and its decomposition $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ into a direct sum of minimal rotation-invariant spaces. We consider elements of $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ as functions of two variables, a nonnegative integer variable $m$ and a complex variable $u$ (a restriction of such function to a set $m=k$ is a polynomial in $u$ of degree $\le 2k$). The group $\mathrm{GL}\,(3,{\mathbb R})$ of all matrices of order 3 acts on $S^2$, so its Lie algebra acts in $C^\infty(S^2)$ by differentiations along vector fields. We construct operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$ corresponding such differentiations and obtain a collection of differential-difference operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$. The expressions include shifts $m\mapsto m\pm 2$ and derivatives of order 4 in $u$.

title: Optimal power concavity of the variational mean curvature via singular $1$-Laplace problems
abstract: Let $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded convex domain and let $H_Ω\leq 0$ denote its variational mean curvature, in the sense of Barozzi, Gonzalez and Tamanini [PAMS, 1987]. We prove that $-H_Ω$ is harmonic convex, that is $1/H_Ω$ is a convex function in $Ω$, and that the exponent $-1$ is optimal in the class of convex domains. This strictly improves the concavity of $H_Ω$ obtained by Alter and Caselles [Nonlinear Anal., 2009], who also proved, by geometric methods, a closely related property for the classical mean curvature under Minkowski interpolation of convex bodies. Our approach is analytic: the result is deduced from a concavity property of the solution of the singular $1$-Laplace Dirichlet problem $$\begin{cases} -Δ_1 u = {u^{-γ}} & \quad \hbox{in $Ω$}, \\ u = 0 &\quad \hbox{on $\partial Ω$}, \end{cases}$$ for $γ\in (0,1]$, whose unique positive solution is $u=(-H_Ω)^{-1/γ}$. We show that $u^γ$ is concave, and we obtain this by proving that the solutions $u_p$ of the approximating problems $-Δ_p u_p = u_p^{-γ}$ are $\frac{p-1+γ}{p}$-concave on every bounded convex domain, without any boundary regularity, and then letting $p\to 1^+$. Explicit examples show that no Hölder continuity of $H_Ω$ up to $\partialΩ$ holds uniformly in the class of convex domains with $C^{1,1}$ boundary.

title: Manifold-Informed Neural Networks for Low-Label ECG Electrolyte Inference
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) supervise on the residual of a known differential operator. Many high-stakes inference problems admit no such operator: clinical signals, behavioral measurements, materials properties. We introduce the Manifold-Informed Neural Network (MINN), a PINN-parallel paradigm that replaces the physics operator residual with a manifold operator residual: a discrete Poisson equation $\mathbf{L}_G \mathbf{H} = s_ϕ(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{m})$ on a $k$-nearest-neighbor graph in the learned latent space, with a learned, task-aware source. The construction is a structural parallel to PINNs (squared operator residual plus label data, in place of operator residual plus boundary data); the $s{=}0$ limit recovers the homogeneous Laplace equation $\mathbf{L}_G\mathbf{H}=\mathbf{0}$ (classical manifold regularization solves the same equation but minimizes the Dirichlet energy $\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{H}^\top\mathbf{L}_G\mathbf{H})$, a different penalty form). The source $s_ϕ$ takes input features and auxiliary metadata directly, breaking the homogeneous smoothness prior that limits classical Laplacian penalties; gated Feature-wise Linear Modulation separately fuses metadata into the prediction branch. We evaluate MINN on three-class classification of potassium, calcium, and magnesium from 12-lead ECGs in MIMIC-IV-ECG, against twelve baselines spanning supervised and tabular methods, ECG foundation models, and manifold/graph approaches. MINN attains the highest K$^+$ Macro-F1 of 0.61 (best baseline 0.55), with consistent gains on Ca$^{2+}$ and Mg$^{2+}$ and a 31% relative improvement at 1% labeled data. Six targeted ablations show that the inhomogeneous Poisson formulation, not graph smoothing alone, drives the gain.

title: PACE: Plan, Attend, Check, and Emit for Training-Free Response Timing in Streaming Video Understanding
abstract: Streaming video understanding requires a model to decide not only what to answer but also when to answer. Evidence arrives progressively, and recent benchmarks identify premature responses, issued before the queried event has concluded, as a recurring failure mode. Existing approaches often learn response timing through additional training, while training-free alternatives typically rely on scalar gating signals that do not explicitly represent when an answer becomes final. We organize chunk-wise streaming errors into three patterns: sampling variation can make an answer unstable, a stable answer may lack support in the observed video, or an answer may be supported by the current evidence while the event remains unfinished. We propose PACE (Plan, Attend, Check, and Emit), a training-free framework designed around these three failure modes. Given a question, PACE drafts a plan specifying what to observe and what will signal completion. As the stream unfolds, it invokes an off-the-shelf video LLM at informative moments, evaluates each draft for stability, grounding in its cited frames, and completion, and records verified observations in an event ledger. Experiments on ProactiveVideoQA and OVO-Bench Forward show that PACE improves over the official protocols by up to 5.9 average PAUC points and 6.2 average accuracy points across proprietary and open-source backbones, yielding state-of-the-art performance.

title: Latency-Neutral Passive Cyber Monitoring for Grid-Edge Operational Technology Networks
abstract: Deterministic industrial networks often present an operational trade-off between maintaining microsecond timing of primary control loops and capturing security telemetry. This work investigates the engineering feasibility of the Operational Technology Supervisor (OTSV), a three-tier passive monitoring framework designed to resolve this visibility challenge within timing-sensitive grid-edge infrastructure. By utilizing a Layer-3-unconfigured passive ingestion mode on bare-metal hardware via a physical switched port analyzer (SPAN) loop, the deep packet inspection engine is isolated from the production network, implementing a software-enforced unidirectional export policy. Performance validation conducted over a continuous audit comprising 32,927 active-monitoring round-trip time (RTT) samples yielded stable latency distributions across a laboratory power-monitoring loop running Modbus TCP and IEC 61850 MMS protocols. The measured latency delta between the unmonitored baseline and the active monitoring state was less than 0.12 milliseconds, supporting the feasibility of continuous high-fidelity security observation alongside stringent grid-edge metering timing bounds without measurably degrading the monitored reporting path.

title: Is Sycophancy a Form of In-Context Updating?
abstract: Factual sycophancy, a language model's deference to a user's false beliefs, is usually understood as a bid for the user's approval at the expense of truthfulness. We argue that this framing over-emphasizes the user and propose viewing sycophancy as a failure within the broader and generally useful process of in-context updating, by which models revise their answers based on information supplied during an interaction. We support this view with behavioral and mechanistic evidence. First, models' responses to user claims sit within a broader pattern of source-sensitive updating. They revise their answers in response to information attributed to external sources as well, more so when it appears better supported, and their deference to the user persists even when no user approval is at stake. Second, the internal components that support deference to the user are also causally important for in-context updating more broadly. Our results suggest that factual sycophancy arises when in-context updating gives a user's assertion excessive weight relative to its evidence. Because sycophancy is embedded in this process, reducing it risks reducing useful updating as well, a trade-off that calls for evaluations measuring both behaviors and mitigations that decouple them.

title: Electronic driving of torsional modes in carbon nanotubes via orbital-phonon coupling
abstract: We theoretically investigate electronic driving of a torsional mode in a suspended carbon nanotube quantum dot. The valley states in a nanotube carry opposite orbital magnetic moments along the tube axis, and intervalley mixing forms valley-mixed eigenstates whose splitting can be controlled by an axial magnetic field. We formulate an orbital-rotation coupling between the torsional angular velocity and the valley orbital angular momentum. Using a master equation for sequential tunneling through normal-metal electrodes, we calculate the steady-state current and the phonon distribution of the torsional mode. When the valley-state splitting matches the torsional phonon energy, orbital transitions can drive the mode out of equilibrium. The contacts control both phonon pumping and its electrical readout, allowing substantial excitation with a positive, vanishing, or negative current response. The mechanism requires no intrinsic spin or valley polarization of the electrodes, but uses state-dependent tunneling at the contacts.

title: Observation Assimilation Transformer: Probabilistic Weather Analysis from Sparse Station Observations
abstract: We present the Observation Assimilation Transformer (OAT), a geometry-aware neural process that corrects and refines a prior numerical weather prediction (NWP) field into a high-resolution posterior field by assimilating sparse observations. OAT is an encoder-decoder transformer that considers a set of observed locations and their NWP prior to condition predictions at a set of arbitrary unobserved query locations. Its sparse attention mechanism makes it scalable to thousands of station observations and depends on relative positions between locations, never on the absolute coordinates. The model allows for partially missing observations, predictions at arbitrary continuous locations without grid projection, and outputs are parametric distributions. A station-randomized training algorithm is developed with continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) loss. We test OAT on two datasets - one at regional scale with hundreds of stations, and one at continental scale with thousands of stations. On these datasets OAT outperforms several baselines and shows well calibrated predictions. In an illustrative case study, OAT's downscaling capabilities are demonstrated by downscaling ERA5 (~31km) to COSMO (1km), where OAT achieves lower mean absolute error (MAE) and CRPS for temperature and precipitation on test stations compared to COSMO.

title: A Joint Local Limit Theorem for Prime Divisor Counting Functions
abstract: We establish a uniform two-dimensional local limit theorem for the joint distribution of $Ω(n)$ and $Ω(n+1)$. More precisely, along a set of scales of logarithmic density one, the normalized joint counts are uniformly approximated by the density of two independent Gaussian random variables, each with mean and variance $\log\log x$, up to a power-saving error. The proof builds upon a recent circle-method framework of Tao and Teräväinen. Our results equally hold for the additive function $ω$. Additionally, we explore applications of our local limit theorem in the setting of uniquely ergodic systems.

title: Reinforced Iterative Learning Control for elastic joint arms: Guaranteed cross-trajectory generalization under model uncertainties
abstract: Trajectory tracking for compliant robots is challenging due to nonlinear dynamics and modeling uncertainties, often requiring learning-based methods to avoid explicit parameter identification. Iterative Learning Control (ILC) ensures theoretically high precision and preserves the passive compliance of the robot. However, traditional ILC requires a separate learning phase for each new trajectory. Conversely, Reinforcement Learning (RL) generalizes to new trajectories, but practically suffers from high sample complexity and limited tracking precision. This work proposes Reinforced Iterative Learning Control (RILC) that combines the strengths of both approaches to achieve fast adaptation and guaranteed tracking convergence across diverse trajectories. By establishing a concurrent coupling between the two controllers, RILC overcomes the high initial errors and slow adaptation of traditional ILC, enabling high-performance tracking from the very first trials. In this architecture, ILC provides high-quality samples, while RL contributes as a generalizing best-effort policy across iterations. Additionally, a theoretical proof is presented to show that the RL component preserves ILC stability and, under specific conditions, can also reduce the error bound asymptotically. The efficacy of this framework is demonstrated through simulation and experiments on an underactuated 4-degree-of-freedom serial elastic robot using different trajectories and modeling mismatches.

title: Identifying Dependent Components from Multi-domain Linear Mixtures
abstract: We study a linear mixing model with dependent latent components, assuming multiple data domains. Most existing models assume that the components are independent or at least uncorrelated, in line with independent component analysis (ICA). Some recent work allows for dependent components, but then makes specific assumptions such as parametric forms of dependencies, multi-view settings, or interventions, or does not recover the individual components. In contrast, we consider a multi-domain setting in which domains differ through domain-specific scalings of the components, while the distribution of the underlying latent components is the same across domains. This approach can model data collected, for example, from different sensors measuring the same process, different laboratories conducting the same experiment, different experimental conditions, or different subjects that might differ in biological or physiological factors. We show that, under sufficient domain variability, latent variables and mixing functions can be identified from second-order statistics alone. We propose the Multi-Domain Covariance Matching (MuDo-CoM) algorithm that generalizes previous methods of joint diagonalization. MuDo-CoM is validated on simulated data and a real-world fMRI dataset.

title: Coevolution of Dust Growth and Gravitational Instability in Massive Protostellar Disks
abstract: Massive protostellar disks are expected to sustain high accretion rates through gravitational instability, while dust growth may modify their opacity, cooling efficiency, and stability. Conversely, the time-dependent and nonaxisymmetric structures produced by gravitational instability may regulate the local conditions for dust growth. However, the coupled evolution of dust growth and gravitational instability in massive protostellar disks has not yet been explored self-consistently. We present two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations that follow gas dynamics, dust growth, and opacity-dependent radiative cooling in a massive protostellar disk. We find that dust grains rapidly grow to millimeter-centimeter sizes shortly after disk formation, substantially reducing the infrared opacity. The enhanced cooling promotes disk fragmentation and produces more frequent accretion-driven luminosity outbursts than in a model without dust growth, with durations and peak luminosities comparable to those observed in massive protostars. Dust growth is broadly regulated by the fragmentation-limited size in dense disk regions, whereas newly formed outer disk regions and low-density regions deviate from this limit because of finite collision timescales and dust transport. These results suggest that dust growth may facilitate episodic accretion and fragmentation, while gravitationally unstable disk structures in turn regulate the dust growth process.

title: RECAP: Representation-Based Calibration with Amortized Pooling for Frequentist Simulation-Based Inference
abstract: Simulation-based inference enables uncertainty quantification in broad contexts when a simulation model is available but when a test statistic's sampling distribution is not tractable. But, frequentist calibration in this setting can be costly over high-dimensional parameter spaces. In this paper, we introduce RECAP (REpresentation-based Calibration with Amortized Pooling), a general framework for frequentist simulation-based inference. RECAP exploits low-dimensional structure in how the null distribution varies with parameters and is particularly useful when the parameter dimension is high or when different parameter configurations have redundant or compensating effects. RECAP pools simulated scores according to a representation that preserves this distribution exactly or approximately, allowing distant parameter values to share calibration information. Representations may be derived from model structure or learned independently. Empirical quantiles of the pooled scores then yield tests and confidence sets, for which we establish theoretical coverage guarantees. In the simulation studies, we show that RECAP has lower coverage error than existing approaches and power close to that of the point-wise oracle, while maintaining the computational benefits of amortized calibration. An application to population genomics illustrates learned low-dimensional calibration and interpretable uncertainty quantification.

title: Ensemble basis-free coherence for quantum communication
abstract: The resource theory of coherence quantifies the quantum properties of states and their role in quantum information processing. Extending coherence theory to ensembles, the natural objects in quantum communication, remains an active research direction, with their operational potential still being explored. In this work, we establish a maximally coherent ensemble in every finite dimension: the continuous ensemble of pure states distributed according to the normalized Haar measure attains the tight upper bound on basis-free relative entropy ensemble coherence. We then prove that ensemble coherence bounds the effective informational advantage of postselective measurements over the Holevo quantity for two equiprobable pure states. Finally, for the qubit B92 QKD protocol, we show that the coherence of Alice's ensemble upper-bounds the secret key rate in the asymptotic regime. These results give ensemble coherence a quantitative operational meaning in quantum communication and cryptography

title: Spin-wave circulation in unbounded ferromagnetic film
abstract: A key challenge in spin-wave computing is steering spin waves through circuits without wave distortion or reflections. This often results in 1D propagation scenarios, which hinder applicability in 2D magnonic circuits. We demonstrate experimentally a novel approach using a hard magnetic spherical microparticle to guide spin-waves onto a closed path in a plain thin YIG film. The particle stray field induces a radially symmetrical magnetization landscape, which allows spin-waves to loop around. In parallel, we conducted micromagnetic simulations reproducing the experimental conditions, which confirm the circulation of spin-waves over several loops around the particle. This work demonstrates the possibility to steer spin-waves onto a circular path using inhomogeneous magnetic landscape, as well as advancing scalable spin-wave-based information processing technologies.

title: First-Order Mean Field Games with Time-Measurable and $C ^{1,1}$ Hamiltonians: Analysis and Approximation
abstract: We introduce and analyze a numerical framework for a class of first-order, non-local Mean Field Game (MFG) systems with two sources of low regularity: the time-dependent data are merely measurable, and the Hamiltonian is only of class $C^{1,1}$ with respect to the momentum variable. The proposed method combines a semi-Lagrangian approximation of the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation with a Lagrange--Galerkin discretization of the continuity equation. Temporal measurability is handled by averaging the data over the time-grid intervals and using the stability theory of $L^1$-viscosity solutions. The limited regularity of the Hamiltonian is addressed through arguments from nonsmooth analysis, based in particular on Clarke's generalized differential calculus. We prove that the discrete solutions converge, up to some subsequence, to a solution of the MFG system. As a consequence, the numerical approximation also provides a constructive existence result. Under a monotonicity assumption on the coupling terms, we show that the solution to the MFG system is unique, implying the convergence of the whole sequence of discrete solutions. Finally, numerical experiments in one and two spatial dimensions illustrate the robustness of the method, including a linear--quadratic example with a running cost that is discontinuous in time and for which we compute an exact solution.

title: Floquet ground state order
abstract: Clean, interacting, periodically driven systems are believed to thermalize to featureless, infinite-temperature states that preclude the formation of stable ordered states. Here, we show stable quantum order, distinct from prethermal order, and its phase transitions in the ground state of the average-energy operator. Decomposing the time evolution into geometric and average-energy dynamics, we apply Geometric Floquet theory to identify the Floquet ground state. We derive a general variational principle to compute the Floquet ground state in large interacting periodically driven systems, and use it to develop a matrix product state algorithm.
