Dual-energy (DE) chest radiography may enable accessible opportunistic CAC assessment by separating calcifications from overlapping bone. Purpose: To evaluate multi-task deep learning for CAC localization and CT-referenced score prediction and assess projection, image representation, and exposure effects. Methods: This retrospective simulation study used 550 calcium-scoring CT exams with reference CAC masks and Agatston scores. Dual-layer DE radiographs were simulated with a physics-based detector model. A modified nnU-Net jointly predicted CAC localization and scores from continuous probability maps. Comparisons included AP, 45°, and lateral views; lateral single-energy (SE), DE bone, and high-pass filtered DE bone images; and dose-matched models at 70, 50, and 24 mAs. Patient-level splitting reserved 10% for independent testing; five-fold models provided averaged inference. Metrics included Dice and AUC at CAC thresholds >0, >100, >400, and >1000, with bootstrap uncertainty and paired DeLong tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction. Results: Lateral views achieved Dice 0.34 versus 0.23 (AP) and 0.22 (45°), with AUCs for CAC >100 of 0.86, 0.81, and 0.77, respectively; AUC differences were not significant after correction. Lateral DE bone outperformed SE (Dice: 0.33 vs. 0.19; AUC for CAC >100: 0.86 vs. 0.64), with significant AUC advantages at >100, >400, and >1000. High-pass filtering added little classification benefit. Dice decreased with exposure, while AUC differences across doses were not significant. Conclusions: Simulation results support lateral dual-layer DE bone imaging for opportunistic CAC assessment, with significant advantages over SE. Physical and clinical validation is needed.

title: Real-analytic standard families and rotational invariant curves
abstract: In this paper we study one-parameter families of exact standard maps of the form $$\widehat{f}_{k,g}(\widehat{x},\widehat{y}) =\bigl(\widehat{x}+\widehat{y}+kg(\widehat{x}) \bmod 1,\widehat{y}+kg(\widehat{x})\bigr),$$ where $k$ is a real parameter and $g:\mathbb{T} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is real-analytic, 1-periodic and has zero mean. The most famous example is when $g(\widehat{x})=\frac{\sin(2π\widehat{x})}{2π}$. In this case, the closed subset $A_{\sin(2π\cdot)/(2π)}\subset \mathbb{R}$ of values of $k$ for which $\widehat{f}_{k,\sin(2π\cdot)/(2π)}$ has rotational invariant curves is conjectured to be a closed interval. Much has been done towards this conjecture, both numerically and analytically. But a complete proof has not yet been achieved. Our approach here goes in the opposite direction: we construct a function $θ:\mathbb{T} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the above conditions, such that $A_θ$ is not an interval: It contains at least 2 different connected components, which are non-degenerate closed intervals.

title: Hyperbolic comparison and rigidity for the hyperspherical radius
abstract: We prove Gromov's hyperbolic hyperspherical radius comparison and rigidity conjectures in all dimensions $n\ge3$, without the spin assumption. Let $(X^n, g)$ be a smooth, oriented, connected, compact Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth connected boundary $S$. If ${\rm Sc}_g\ge -n(n-1)$ and $H_S\ge (n-1)\coth R$ for some $R>0$, then ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)\le\sinh R$, with equality if and only if $(X^n,g)$ is isometric to the closed hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$. Under the same curvature bounds, every smooth $1$-Lipschitz map of nonzero degree from $S$ to the boundary of the hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$ extends to an isometry of the fillings. Here, $g_S$ is the induced boundary metric, $H_S$ is the mean curvature of $S$ with respect to the outward unit normal, and ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)$ denotes the hyperspherical radius.

title: Finite-range hair from a nonlocal matter sector: charged Yukawa black holes
abstract: { We construct a new exact charged, static and spherically symmetric black-hole solution of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with an additional anisotropic matter sector, whose metric is the Reissner--Nordström geometry endowed with a Yukawa-type contribution. The Yukawa term is exponentially screened: it is visible in the strong-field region but carries no independent asymptotic charge. We obtain an analytic parametrization of the extremal curve, identify the condition for higher-order degenerate horizons, characterize the curvature singularity and establish the weak, null, dominant and strong energy conditions. We further study the horizon thermodynamics, including the conjugate variables associated with the amplitude and range of the Yukawa sector and the corresponding generalized Smarr relation. The photon sphere, shadow, ray-traced appearance and quasinormal ringdown are then analyzed, with quasinormal frequencies computed through the sixth-order WKB expansion and confirmed, overtones included, by an independent spectral method. {Confronting the model shadow with Event Horizon Telescope measurements of M87* and Sgr A* constrains the finite-range sector directly, favoring its strongly screened, near-Reissner--Nordström regime.} This provides a unified geometric and phenomenological characterization of finite-range charged black-hole hair in ordinary Einstein gravity. }

title: MythoSemantic: An Interactive System for Discovering Semantic Parallels Across Mythological and Religious Traditions
abstract: We present a tool for the comparative study of mythological and religious texts. Traditional manual analysis is highly labor-intensive and difficult to scale. To address this, we use neural language models to embed texts into a shared semantic space, so that users can find semantic parallels across cultural traditions in an interactive interface. Embedded fragments form distinct semantic structures whose coarse geometry aligns with well-documented historical relations between traditions. We quantify how much of that geometry is already explained by lexical overlap and by proper names. The current system is available at https://mythoscope.io, and the installable package is available at https://github.com/haafus/MythoSemantic/blob/main/RUN.md.

title: Quantum Simulation of the Static Yukawa Model via Effective Particles on a Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulator
abstract: Trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and circuit QED quantum computers naturally enable coupled qubit-boson simulations. Boson-fermion interactions arise in quantum field theory, where renormalization is required to obtain finite results. We study one of the simplest examples of a coupled fermion-boson system, the static Yukawa model, on the QSCOUT trapped-ion system. We use similarity renormalization to express the same physics in terms of effective particles described by different values of the renormalization parameter $s$. This enables us to map data taken in the window of bosonic occupancy that is experimentally accessible to larger occupancies of distinct effective particles. We use this to study strongly coupled, high-occupancy regimes despite limited readout ranges. Using a trapped-ion qubit-boson device on Sandia National Laboratories' QSCOUT platform, we demonstrate the time evolution of the static Yukawa model.

title: Toolflation: Seller Agents Distort Tool Markets Through Spontaneous Generative Engine Optimization
abstract: Agents are starting to sell to other agents. Seller agents write the listings of tools, services and products, and buyer agents read these listings when they choose what to use. We show that seller agents told only to be selected more often practice generative engine optimization on their own, and that this distorts the market for sellers and for buyers. We build tool markets from real data tools on Amazon and Instagram and run every tool on every question, so we know which tools can answer each question. Under all five production models we test, sellers rewrite their descriptions to claim more and more fields, including fields that their tools return for fewer than half of the targets. We call this process toolflation. Nothing in the market limits it, and how far it goes depends on the model, as the number of claims that contradict the sellers' own evidence differs by an order of magnitude between models. Toolflation shifts the buyers' choices between sellers, and the most capable tool loses share in seven of the ten combinations of seller model and platform. Under four models, the choices stay with capable tools and buyer agents keep their task success. Under the fifth, sellers copy one another until the descriptions no longer tell the tools apart. Buyer agents then pick tools by their position in the list, tools that answer almost nothing win a quarter to two fifths of the choices, and task success falls from 89% to about 30% on Amazon, close to random choice, and from 77% to 40% on Instagram. The sellers did only what their vendors asked, and the cost fell on buyers they never dealt with. We therefore argue that honesty toward third parties under competition is part of safety alignment, and that models should be tested as sellers before they are deployed as sellers.

title: A Bochner Weitzenböck Decomposition for Cellular Sheaf Laplacians, Curvature and Neural Sheaf Diffusion
abstract: We extend the Bochner-Weitzenböck decomposition to cellular sheaf Laplacians, splitting it into a positive semidefinite term, the Bochner sheaf Laplacian, and a block diagonal term, the Forman curvature. We show that the Bochner Laplacians form a class of cellular sheaves that extends both connection and matrix-weighted Laplacians, and generalizes signed graphs to $d$ dimensions. We give a holonomy characterization of their kernel, prove the related Cheeger inequalities, and attach to them a random walk that generalizes the Gremban expansion. For the Forman term, we prove a discrete Bochner theorem, which bounds the first cohomology of a cellular sheaf with nonnegative curvature, and we read the whole decomposition as an opinion-dynamics model. We then apply this machinery to Sheaf Neural Networks, whose learnt Laplacian is otherwise unobserved. The Bochner interpretation yields a node-level conviction score that acts as an operational importance measure under frozen-model interventions, while the Forman profile provides a local descriptor of the learnt operator.

title: Existence of Ulrich bundles on polarized surfaces and weakly Ulrich bundles on polarized varieties in positive characteristic
abstract: In their seminal paper \cite{eisenbud2003resultants}, Eisenbud and Schreyer asked whether every smooth projective variety admits an Ulrich bundle with respect to each very ample polarization. This question has stimulated extensive research for more than two decades. Recently, Anghel \cite{anghel2026smooth} constructed counterexamples over $\mathbb C$ in dimension two, and Lopez \cite{lopez2026existence} extended this nonexistence result to higher dimensions. In this article, we study the existence problem for sufficiently large multiples of a fixed polarization and derive applications in positive characteristic. Over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, we prove that every polarized smooth surface admits an Ulrich bundle and every polarized smooth variety admits a weakly Ulrich bundle. Consequently, the Chow forms of surfaces (resp. varieties) admit linear determinantal (resp. determinantal) representations. Moreover, for every such polarized surface, the cone of cohomology tables of coherent sheaves coincides with that on $(\mathbb{P}^2, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1))$.

title: GPT-6-Astra Understands Touch and Outperform Vision--Tactile--Language--Action Models
abstract: General-purpose multimodal models have shown promise as direct robot action policies, yet whether they grasp the physics underlying real-world interactions and can apply that understanding to guide action remains underexplored. We investigate this question using contact-rich manipulation as a representative testbed, examining tactile understanding as a concrete instance of this broader capability. Contact-rich manipulation requires interpreting tactile feedback and adjusting actions after obstruction. Existing learned tactile policies acquire these capabilities through specialized pretraining and per-task optimization, with substantial data and training costs. We present GPT-as-Tactile-Policy, which summarizes expert demonstrations into task guidance and tactile references for contact assessment and corrective action. GPT-6-Astra combines this context with multimodal observations and interaction history to generate control commands and adjust actions through contact feedback. Without additional robotics-specific pretraining or per-task policy fine-tuning, our method achieves 93.8\% mean success across five UniVTAC tasks. Overall performance is comparable to state-of-the-art policies, with higher success on selected tasks. On Insert Hole, tactile feedback improves success from 31\% to 99\%. Execution analysis further demonstrates contact-guided probing and correction, supporting manipulation progress through explicit expert experience and online feedback.

title: LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors
abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) offer an appealing approach to self-supervised learning, but are typically prone to representation collapse. LeJEPA resolves this by introducing a theoretically grounded distribution-matching objective that drives the embedding towards an isotropic Gaussian. However, this approach is fundamentally tied to Euclidean assumptions, and its global target does not reflect domain-specific geometric priors, such as the use of non-Euclidean embedding geometries, e.g., equivariant CNNs or hyperbolic ViTs. We thus introduce LocaLeJEPA, a framework motivated by a manifold-theoretic reformulation of LeJEPA's entropy-maximization property. The accompanying LocaLeReg, a novel locally Euclidean distribution-matching regularizer, enables a stable and scalable implementation of the LocaLeJEPA framework. We then perform extensive experiments in the vision setting on models trained on ImageNet-1K. LocaLeJEPA significantly outperforms LeJEPA when paired with hyperbolic ViT-S/8 and equivariant ResNet-50 backbones, and also with ordinary Euclidean ViT-S/8 and ViT-L/14 backbones. This holds both in terms of linear and k-NN classification performance on ImageNet and on a series of downstream tasks tested. We view the LocaLeJEPA formalism as a principled approach to the JEPA paradigm that better respects intrinsic data geometry while also accommodating generalizations to exotic embedding geometries. Code available at https://github.com/alessioborgi/LocaLeJEPA.

title: A Hierarchical Space-Ground Collaborative Network: Architecture Design and Deployment
abstract: The sixth-generation (6G) landscape demands a profound architectural evolution toward a unified, collaborative ecosystem that integrates satellite and terrestrial segments to provide ubiquitous global connectivity. Nevertheless, conventional independent management paradigms are increasingly challenged by the profound spatiotemporal nonstationarity of low-Earth orbit (LEO) channels and the volatile demands of massive heterogeneous services. To address these challenges, this study focuses on the architectural design of space-ground integrated networks (SGINs) and investigates elastic deployment strategies tailored to heterogeneous 6G service requirements. We first review the development trends in SGIN and then summarize typical application scenarios into two categories, along with their associated challenges and constraints. After that, a hierarchical space-ground collaborative network (SGCN) architecture is proposed to support achieving larger network capability, extensive continuous coverage, and enhanced spectral efficiency, which is evaluated through three representative scenarios with progressive baselines. Subsequently, a service-aware deployment strategy is introduced to further establish the engineering feasibility of the proposed architecture.

title: Linear Axiomatization of Linear Differential Equations
abstract: This article presents an axiomatization of linear differential equations that is complete for topologically open properties with compact initial conditions and time horizons by proving them deductively via a sound reduction to formulas of linear real arithmetic. Indeed, linearity is preserved: linear differential invariants are complete for open properties of linear differential equations and reduce with a linear number of Lie derivatives (per atom) to linear real arithmetic. In particular, this article shows that the linear fragment of differential dynamic logic (dL), a modal extension of standard first-order logic over the reals satisfies these completeness properties. By establishing completeness within decidable linear real arithmetic, the need for proving sophisticated nonlinear formulas of real arithmetic is circumvented. Furthermore, this article establishes generalizations to the nonlinear fragment of dL that enable the practical certification of reachability computations, validating the output of external computations in dL with machine-checkable proofs.

title: Ubiquitous Flat Bands in Edge-Inflated Random Graphs
abstract: Flat bands are usually associated with periodic lattice geometries, where destructive interference or chiral-symmetry constraints produce macroscopically degenerate eigenstates. Here we show that flat bands arise generically in a broad class of nonperiodic random networks through a simple edge-inflation procedure. Starting from random regular, Voronoi tessellation, Delaunay triangulation, scale-free, small-world, and Erdös-Rényi seed graphs, each edge is replaced by a finite one-dimensional tight-binding chain, either with fixed length $L$ or with random lengths of mean $\bar L$. Although the original random graphs typically have adjacency matrices of full rank and therefore few or no zero eigenstates, their inflated counterparts exhibit extensive flat bands. The flat-band energies are determined by the eigenstates residing on the chains or, more generally, by the eigenvalues of identical loopless motifs replacing the seed bonds. The corresponding eigenstates are states supported on subsets of the inflated chains formed by destructive interference at the original seed vertices. For zero-energy flat bands, we relate the degeneracy to the graph nullity $η(G)$ and the maximum matching number $ν(G)$. The numerical results support the correspondence $η(G)=N-2ν(G)$, up to small deviations, across the random graph ensembles studied. The fraction of degenerate zero-energy states in inflated random graphs is controlled primarily by the average degree of the seed graph. We further show that the flat bands exhibit characteristic robustness to disorder: disorder on the seed sites and random magnetic flux leave the flat bands essentially unchanged, while bond disorder and disorder on the chain or motif sites broaden them. These results show that flat bands do not require crystalline order, but can emerge as robust consequences of local graph inflation and motif substitution.

title: Tuning between collective dynamics and scrambling through initial-state symmetry alignment in long-range spin models
abstract: Long-range interactions in many-body quantum systems give rise to a wide range of dynamical phenomena, from collective dynamics well described by integrable mean-field models with symmetric all-to-all couplings, to fast scrambling of quantum information from disordered long-range interactions. Here, we investigate scenarios in which both regimes emerge within a single deterministic, translation-invariant XY spin model with long-range couplings. We consider a sparse powers-of-two (PWR2) graph, where each spin interacts with a logarithmic number of neighbors, and a power-law-decaying model. By altering the initial state via local perturbations on a completely symmetric state, we show that the dynamics changes from collective to scrambling as witnessed by bipartite and multipartite entanglement measures. We characterize this collective-to-scrambling crossover using Lyapunov exponents in the semiclassical regime, and show that the spectral properties of the coupling graph adjacency matrix provide a very efficient tool to predict the onset of fast scrambling. Our results offer a unified framework for controlling the switch between collective and scrambling dynamics in a setup accessible in experiments with neutral atoms in cavities or in tweezer arrays.

title: Backward Homogeneous Heat Equation with $Ψ$-Caputo Time Derivative and Spectral Fractional Laplacian
abstract: In this work, we study a fractional diffusion model in time and space, formulated in an open and bounded domain, involving a Caputo fractional derivative of order $μ\in(0,1)$ with respect to a time scale function $Ψ$, together with a spectral fractional Laplacian operator of order $s\in(0,1)$. The associated direct problem is analyzed, as well as the inverse problem of temporal reconstruction from final data, which is inherently ill-posed. Through a spectral representation, the instability of the problem and the effect of the choice of the function $Ψ$ on the amplification of spectral modes are examined.

title: ACM, almost Ulrich, and Ulrich vector bundles arising from Frobenius
abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$ over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. We investigate ACM, almost Ulrich (both ACM and weakly Ulrich), and Ulrich properties of the sheaves of locally exact and closed $i$-forms $B_X^i$, $Z_X^i$. These cohomological properties are closely related to the fundamental concepts of Frobenius splitting and ordinarity. Joshi studied the sheaf $B^1_X$ in this context in \cite{MR3920911, MR4206787}, including ACM and almost Ulrich twists of $B^1_X$. However, varieties with Ulrich twisted $B_X^1$ have not been classified for $n\ge2$. We classify subcanonical polarized varieties with initialized ACM $B^i_X(aH)$ for $i=1, n$ and prove that, for $n \ge 2$, varieties with ACM $B^i_X$ for all $i \le \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil$ are ordinary. When $X$ is ordinary with trivial $Ω^1_X$, almost Ulrich twists of $B^i_X$ and $F_*^e(Z_X^i(aH))$ are determined. We classify polarized varieties $(X,H)$ with $B_X^i(aH)$ Ulrich when $n=1, 2$, and establish strong necessary criteria for $n \geq 3$, together with an example. We also prove that $Z_X^i(aH)$ is never Ulrich. Finally, we classify polarized abelian varieties with Ulrich $B^1_X \otimes L$ allowing twists by arbitrary line bundles.

title: MARE: An Open-Source Lunar Rover Simulator with Shadow Ground Truth for Perception and Autonomy
abstract: Lunar surface exploration increasingly relies on autonomous rovers that must perceive and traverse unstructured terrain under extreme illumination conditions. Near the lunar poles, low sun elevations produce long, high-contrast shadows that challenge stereo vision, terrain segmentation, and localization. Developing perception and navigation algorithms for these conditions requires large amounts of sensor data with accurate ground truth, which field campaigns and analog facilities can only provide at high cost and with limited variety. This paper presents MARE (Modular Autonomy and Rendering Environment), an open-source simulation suite for lunar rover perception and autonomy built on Unreal Engine 5 and ROS 2. MARE consists of three integrated components. Terrain Studio generates cratered and rocky lunar Digital Elevation Maps (DEMs) to build simulation scenes. A dedicated Unreal Engine project hosts two physics-based rovers with plugins for stereo, lidar, event, and Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) cameras, streaming time-stamped sensor data and pixel-accurate ground truth. Lastly, a Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) stack provides web-based mission control. Validation shows a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.79 between predicted and rendered shadows at low sun elevations, and stereo depth analysis verifies decreased pixel coverage in shadowed regions relative to sunlit terrain.

title: Exact Nonsymmetric Vacuum Magnetic Fields with Nested Toroidal Surfaces
abstract: We give a constructive method for exact vacuum magnetic fields whose lines fill nested toroidal surfaces in ordinary space, without continuous spatial symmetry. Complex potential theory on an algebraic curve, combined with doubly periodic traveling waves from soliton theory, gives closed forms for the field, its potential and a surface label. Free parameters set the rotational transform and the magnetic shear, including exactly constant irrational transform. The same fields are exact potential flows with toroidal stream surfaces, and give stringent tests for standard stellarator codes.

title: Beyond Trajectory Statistics: Community-Consistent Human Mobility Generation via Evolving User-Location Graphs
abstract: Human mobility data are fundamental to Web-based location services and broader urban applications, and mobility generation provides synthetic trajectories when real data are costly or inaccessible. Although recent mobility generators have incorporated collective mobility patterns, they primarily focus on individual trajectories and aggregate population dynamics, leaving evolving community structures formed by user-location interactions insufficiently modeled. In this paper, we study community-consistent human mobility generation. To this end, we formulate mobility generation as the generation of dynamic user-location graphs to model community structures and propose MOTION, a Multi-agent framework for cOmmuniTy-consIstent human mObility geNeration. MOTION consists of user agents, location agents, and a global manager agent. MOTION first detects coherent communities from historical mobility using the Leiden algorithm and extracts community-conditioned interaction priors to guide the generation process. Guided by these priors, the user agents plan mobility, search destination candidates, and infer user movements from the individual view. In parallel, selectively activated location agents infer likely user arrivals from the community view. The manager coordinates both views, diagnoses interactions causing deviations, and attributes targeted reflection signals to revise user decisions, location attraction, and source-user selection. Experiments on two real-world datasets show that MOTION outperforms baselines by at least 4.05% across reported metrics of individual trajectories, population and flow distributions, and community and graph structures. Further analyses confirm its robustness, privacy preservation, and downstream utility. The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MOTION-04C4.

title: Independent transversals in hypergraphs with low codegrees
abstract: We prove that for every fixed $r\geq3$, $k>0$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there is $γ>0$ such that the following holds for all sufficiently large $b$. An $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ whose vertex set is partitioned into parts of size at least $b$ contains at least $\lceil(1-\varepsilon)b\rceil$ pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals, provided that the average degree in each part is at most $kb^{r-1}$ and maximum $j$-codegree $Δ_j(\mathcal H)\leqγb^{r-j}$ for $2\leq j<r$. Under the same average degree, if $q$ is the minimum part size and $Δ_j(\mathcal H)=o(q^{r-j})$ for $2\leq j<r$, the maximum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals is $(1-o(1))q$ as $q\to\infty$. We develop an iterative halving reduction for partitioned hypergraphs to apply the theorem of Delcourt and Postle on matchings avoiding forbidden submatchings.

title: On the stability of displacement energy in toric manifolds
abstract: We present a quantitative exploration of the behaviour of displacement energy of Lagrangians under stabilization. In particular, we completely characterize the displacement behaviour of toric fibres in Fano 4-manifolds. Our approach relates the geometry of the moment polytope's caustic to the structure of the (bulk-deformed) superpotential and to the presence of symmetric probes.

title: Fast Motion Retargeting Pipeline for Scalable Humanoid Robot Learning
abstract: While large-scale human motion capture datasets provide a rich source of demonstrations for humanoid robot learning, retargeting the diverse motions to different humanoid robots remains a nontrivial challenge. Existing kinodynamic trajectory optimization pipelines are computationally expensive and often require manual adjustments per motion. We present FRDV (Fast Retargeting with Dynamics Validation), a scalable framework consisting of rapid constrained kinematic retargeting and an additional dynamics validation pipeline. Its kinematic stage integrates a custom Sequential Quadratic Programming solver, Real-Time Iteration, and parallel chunk-based processing, achieving up to 9,156 frames per second, approximately up to 136 times faster than GMR and ProtoMotions, while robot-specific constraints are incorporated into the optimization to reduce common retargeting artifacts, such as ground penetration and self-collision. For motions requiring additional verification, a contact implicit iLQR controller is utilized to test the retargeted reference under full rigid body dynamics. This dynamics-based validation identifies dynamically infeasible motions and refines contact-related artifacts such as foot floating and foot skating. We evaluate retargeting quality by training motion tracking reinforcement learning policies using several state-of-the-art pipelines and comparing their tracking fidelity and success rates. Furthermore, sim-to-real transfer is demonstrated on a Unitree G1 humanoid. Videos and code are available at: https://daroslab.github.io/frdv/.

title: Overlapping Reserves without a Common Priority: Theory and an Application to School Choice in Chile
abstract: We study matching markets with overlapping reserves governed by heterogeneous priorities. When applicants qualify for multiple reserves, how they are routed can affect reserve utilization and which applicants are admitted. We introduce classify-and-rank choice rules that yield strategy-proof deferred acceptance mechanisms satisfying maximum reserve utilization and priority-respect. We axiomatically characterize our mechanism's admission outcomes for any given classification and reserve order. With two reserve categories, we provide a foundation for the reserve order and establish its distributional implications for access across eligibility groups. Using nine cycles of Chilean school admissions, which feature such reserves, we document reserve-utilization failures under the deployed mechanism and show that their frequency depends sharply on the reserve order. We show how our mechanism can be adapted to Chile's institutional setting to prevent such failures. Under this alternative mechanism, the reserve order generates a distributional pattern across eligibility groups, consistent with our theory.

title: Sum-over-poles framework for quantum embedding to approach the real-frequency axis
abstract: We introduce a real-frequency framework for the quantum embedding of solids, based on sum-over-poles (SOP) representations. We partition the lattice into periodically repeated interacting fragments and derive an embedded Dyson equation for the fragment, to be solved self-consistently. The resulting scheme generalizes the algorithmic-inversion method of our previous work to interacting Hamiltonians and is closely related to dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), especially when an extended impurity problem is introduced. By exploiting the compact pole expansion of the embedding potential, we carry out the self-consistent procedure close to the real axis, which avoids ill-posed analytic continuation. In addition, the SOP representation allows us to introduce a pole-and-residue dynamics, which we use to reach the self-consistent solution. After deriving the method, we benchmark it against exact-diagonalization implementations of DMFT on the one-dimensional Hubbard ring at half filling. The framework offers a natural route to real-space dynamical quantum embedding, for periodic systems as well as for strongly correlated defects in materials.

title: C*-selflessness and $\mathcal{Z}$-stability for Thompson's group $F$
abstract: We prove that the reduced C*-algebra of Thompson's group $F$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and selfless.

title: Answering in the User's Variety: Calibrated Accommodation Pairs for Post-Training
abstract: People adapt how they talk to the person in front of them. However, chat models tend to respond in Standard English regardless of the dialect used by the user. A uniform answer can hide whether training treats these users alike, and output audits cannot tell as well. We trace how each post-training stage, from supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to preference optimization (DPO) and reinforcement learning, changes a model's tendency to match the user, and read what each update prefers from two content-matched replies, one matching the user and one not. Across 10 open model lineages, post-training standardizes replies to every informal cue, yet after adjusting for how likely each reply already was, the DPO update still favours matching British and Australian spelling over AAE and Singlish on 10 lineages, and models still produce AAE features when asked. We then introduce calibrated accommodation pairs (CAP), preference data that reward matching users' dialect density while preserving Standard English for Standard-English users. On a fully open model, CAP raises convergence on features it was not trained on without a detectable increase in dialect for Standard-English users or a cost in instruction following. In contrast, one-sided pairs reach a similar gain only by overshooting the user and imposing dialect. Our findings show that uniform replies can hide selective updates and audits should read the update as well as the output. Code: https://github.com/kouzhizhuo/cap-accommodation.

title: On the Geometry of Low Rank Correlation Matrices
abstract: Correlation matrices of bounded rank form a stratified space whose factor representations lie in a product of spheres. Using the orbit-type description of the rank stratification, we prove that padding factors preserves the Riemannian geometry of each fixed-rank stratum and the intrinsic length metric of every rank-bounded subset. In the reduced model, a Sylvester equation describes the mechanical connection and its horizontal lifts. We derive sectional-curvature formulas and bounds, characterize zero-curvature directions, and determine the connection's holonomy groups. In particular, a flat rank-two connection can have nontrivial dihedral holonomy. For geodesics subject to a rank bound, rank cannot decrease in the interior of a minimizing segment with maximal-rank endpoints; the local excess over the unconstrained quotient distance is controlled by a dimension-independent cubic estimate. Finally, we compute the exact change of measure between quotient Riemannian volume and Euclidean surface volume in the off-diagonal entries. Coarea yields explicit factor densities for both normalized uniform laws.

title: CLOSER: Evidence-Aware Active Visual Verification for Embodied Object-Goal Navigation
abstract: Object-goal navigation (ObjectNav) requires an embodied agent to find an instance of a specified category in an unseen environment and stop near it. The agent typically relies on an object detector but must judge online from a limited egocentric video stream, sometimes a single frame, whether a detected candidate is the target. Detectors often confidently mistake similar objects, such as a sofa for a bed, and stopping at a false positive fails the episode. Prevailing systems also approach candidates greedily, leaving them occluded or partially observed. We present CLOSER, an evidence-aware active verification framework that treats stopping as closed-loop evidence acquisition, coupling vision-language model (VLM) verification with active perception. CLOSER fine-tunes an open-source VLM to label each view of a candidate tracked across frames as target, non-target, or uncertain, selects complementary views with an embedding-based diversity gate, and fuses their per-view probabilities with a lightweight network. If the fused judgment remains uncertain, a diffusion policy drives the agent toward the candidate using only the tracked mask and depth until the decision becomes decisive. CLOSER runs locally and plugs into existing ObjectNav systems without retraining them. On Gibson and Habitat-Matterport 3D, it raises average success rate by 3.6 points and success weighted by path length by 2.0 points, showing that verifying evidence before committing improves embodied navigation.

title: Counting Bessel zeros and applications
abstract: We establish o-minimal definability results and develop point-counting machinery applicable to the zeros of a Bessel function of fixed non-negative real parameter. We also give an Ax-Schanuel theorem for Bessel functions of fixed (complex) parameters and exponential functions. We combine these to prove a sparsity result (weak Manin-Mumford) for points on an algebraic variety whose coordinates are zeros of a Bessel function of fixed (non-negative real) parameter. We apply this result to improve density results on spectral sets for the unit ball motivated by Fuglede's conjecture.

title: A single generation theorem for simple unital $C^*$-algebras with CPoU and comparison
abstract: In this note, assuming the finite factor generation theorem obtained by OpenAI, we demonstrate that if a separable simple unital $C^*$-algebra $A$ with nonempty trace space, has the strict comparison for positive elements, and its uniform tracial completion has complemented partitions of unity (CPoU), then $A$ is singly generated.

title: Claims of emergence in AI should be grounded in information decomposition
abstract: When a language model develops capabilities not traceable to its individual components, when a multi-agent AI system outperforms each agent on its own, or when a human-AI pair succeeds where either fails in isolation, AI researchers describe it as a case of ``synergy'' or ``emergence''. However, these are usually informal assessments not supported by a theoretical framework, making these claims impossible to compare or even meaningfully dispute. Here we argue that \emph{information decomposition can serve as a unifying formal framework to operationalize assessments about synergy in AI systems}. Information decomposition provides a way to distinguish qualitatively different \emph{types} of information, including unique information available from individual components, redundant information shared across multiple components, and synergistic information accessible only from parts taken together. This gives claims of emergence a precise, falsifiable criterion: a system's behavior is emergent only if it carries synergistic information about task-relevant outcomes. We apply this lens to attention heads, autonomous agents, and human-AI teams, showing how it organizes existing knowledge across scales and substrates, while also generating cross-level conjectures that siloed fields would miss.

title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
abstract: Tracking large human-motion datasets has become the dominant route to general, expressive humanoid whole-body control, but scaling across many motions is expensive. Current pipelines use model-free reinforcement learning, either merging per-motion specialists through lossy distillation, or brute-forcing a single policy with cluster-scale compute. SuperMimic amortizes learning across all motions with one differentiable world model of their shared dynamics, fit from logged transitions of a standard rigid-body simulator. The world model and the tracking policy train together in one loop, and backpropagation-through-time over short imagined rollouts gives the policy analytic gradients. Fast imagined rollouts and analytic gradients make policy learning efficient. In 3 hours on a single GPU, SuperMimic surpasses the return of a state-of-the-art motion tracker baseline trained for 7 days on 128 GPUs. It reduces GPU-hours by more than $1000\times$ and fails on only 25 of 129,514 benchmark motions, versus 179 failures for the baseline. After 9.8 hours on two GPUs, SuperMimic achieves zero failures. From 1 to 264 hours of motion, the world model's prediction error stays stable, and GPU-hours to a target return grow slowly. Our policy transfers to a physical Unitree G1 across diverse and acrobatic motions. SuperMimic removes compute as the bottleneck to scaling humanoid whole-body control, making it practical to measure motion-tracking scaling laws.

title: Liouville Theorems for Semilinear Parabolic Equations Involving the Nonlinear Gradient Term
abstract: In this paper, we prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^q$ via the integral Bernstein method, where $q=2p/(p+1)$ is critical and $M<0$. As an application, we can establish a universal priori estimate for this equation by using the doubling lemma. These results generalize the previous work of Liang and Zhang. We can also prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^2$, which corresponds to the supercritical case.

title: The "Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery" Workshop: A Community Roadmap for the Future of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory After the LSST
abstract: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory will complete its ten-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) in the mid-2030s. Its 8.4 m aperture and 9.6 square degree field of view give it an étendue unmatched by any facility planned for that era. The Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery workshop (KIPAC/SLAC, 3-5 August 2026) brought together approximately 100 participants to discuss Rubin's future after LSST. This paper summarizes the workshop's structure and discussions across five working groups. The continued-surveying group explored a machine-learning foundation model pretrained on Rubin imaging for detection, deblending, and classification. The cadence group considered allocating post-LSST observing time and strategies for transiting exoplanets, Type Ia supernova cosmology, time-delay cosmography, and second-scale transients. The filter group explored broadband, medium-band, and narrowband filters for photometric redshifts, high-redshift large-scale structure, AGN reverberation mapping, Galactic archaeology, and emission-line imaging. The multi-messenger group explored follow-up of next-generation gravitational-wave and neutrino sources, including standard sirens, kilonovae, and Galactic supernovae. The technology group organized options by cost and lead time, including fast readout, new filters, a faster shutter, and summit edge computing. Cross-cutting topics included AI/ML, Chilean and Latin-American co-leadership, satellite megaconstellations, and weather and climate trends at Cerro Pachón. White papers and workshop talks are available through https://zenodo.org/communities/rubin2036workshop/ and https://rubin-observatory.github.io/Rubin-Beyond-LSST/pages/Rubin2036proceedings/.

title: Exploring Temporal Context-Aware Physical Grounding in Latent World Models
abstract: Learning latent dynamics is fundamental to building action-conditioned world models for planning. Among existing families, Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) offer a natural framework by modeling transitions directly in latent space rather than at the pixel level. However, two issues remain in JEPA-based world models: (i) physical grounding lacks explicit aggregation of temporal context and (ii) action planning always overly relies on generic sampling distributions. To this end, we propose $\mathcal{G}$-JEPA, which incorporates temporal context into physical grounding for latent world models and couples the learned models with prior-guided action planning. Specifically, during learning, we incorporate a shared causal temporal module that aggregates temporal context within observation and prediction sequences under physical state supervision, grounding both in task-relevant physical states. When planning, we further introduce action inference through stepwise conditioning of a generative action distribution on the current and goal latent representations together with their evolving discrepancy, yielding anchored proposals that guide model-based online refinement. Together, physical state supervision guides temporal representation learning, while the action prior guides search through the learned world model. Experiments demonstrate improved planning performance on manipulation tasks, including tasks with increasing temporal separation between initial and goal observations. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/myl11045/G-JEPA.

title: Proof-Carrying Contracts: Commitments AI Agents Cannot Break
abstract: AI agents increasingly act on behalf of people or other agents, purchasing services, exchanging information and delegating work. What an agent must respect is written in instructions, policies or agreements, but text alone cannot make it comply. It may make mistakes, be redirected by what it reads, or pursue different interests. For an economy of such agents to function, parties need agreements they can rely on without inspecting or trusting one another's agents. We introduce Proof-Carrying Contracts (PC2), a framework for making agreed constraints enforceable throughout an agent's interactions with a system. Before a requested operation can run, the agent must supply a machine-checkable proof that it preserves the agreed constraints in every case allowed by its model. An execution system called the Airlock checks the proof and controls access to the operation. The parties specify the conditions to preserve, while the agent supplies the reasoning needed to justify its decisions and remains free to adapt its strategy. This avoids having to design a separate permission policy and prove that every decision it permits is safe. We prove that the constraints hold at every instant during execution, even for an adversarial agent, and identify when this implies safety in the world. Reusable capability modules provide tools and guarantees from which contracts can be constructed. PC2 provides a foundation for an agent economy whose agreements protect both those delegating work and those carrying it out.

title: A Solar Optical Clock
abstract: Precision spectroscopy underpins quantum sensing, atomic timekeeping, and the search for terrestrial-mass exoplanets. Finding an Earth-Sun analog requires fractional splitting of spectral features that rivals the precision of the best laboratory spectroscopy. This corresponds to resolution of a few parts in $10^5$ of a typical stellar spectral line, or a Doppler velocity precision of less than 10 cm s$^{-1}$. Only a few astrophysical spectrometers reach this regime, and only by dispersing starlight with large gratings and averaging thousands of lines. Here, we show that comparable precision can be achieved on a single solar line by leveraging techniques used in quantum sensors and optical clocks. A laser is frequency-locked to the 1565 nm solar Fe I line by coupling to a single mode of the solar thermal field and counted against an optical frequency comb referenced to the SI second, thus creating a solar optical clock. Operating at the fundamental photon-noise limit of thermal heterodyne spectroscopy, we achieve centroid precision of one part in $10^9$ of the optical frequency, or 30 cm s$^{-1}$ in radial velocity. We recover the Sun's five-minute acoustic oscillations and the expected Rossiter-McLaughlin signal during a solar eclipse. Combining these techniques from quantum sensing with a thirty-meter-class telescope could enable our demonstrated precision on the nearest Sun-like stars in a few hours. Multiplexing such absolute frequency measurements across lines with different magnetic sensitivity and formation depth would reduce averaging time and help disentangle stellar granulation and activity from the Doppler signature of terrestrial exoplanets, providing new approaches to address some of the most demanding measurements in astrophysical spectroscopy.

title: Reduced graph-based representations of detonation-containing flows
abstract: A graph neural network (GNN)-based autoencoder is leveraged to produce reduced latent graph representations of detonation-containing flows. In a two-dimensional hydrogen-air channel configuration with a uniform fuel-air mixture, it was found that latent graphs with effective resolutions of twice the induction length are capable of reconstructing both the wavefront and the post-shock region of the cellular detonation wave structure. Extrapolation studies using stratified and three-dimensional detonation configurations revealed an intrinsic property of GNN-based reconstruction from reduced latent graphs -- a representational hierarchy, rooted in the local nature of message passing, that tends to prioritize features at the detonation front (i.e., the wavefront profile and triple points) over the downstream deflagrative regions. In particular, it was found that at a fixed ambient condition, the information contained in uniform two-dimensional detonations was sufficient to reconstruct the wavefront structure of both stratified and three-dimensional detonations. Overall, this work demonstrates the utility of GNNs for both reduction and information overlap extraction in detonation-containing flows, opening promising pathways for accelerated simulations of these flows.

title: Geometry-Agnostic Data-Driven Discovery of Extreme Scenarios
abstract: We introduce a two-stage data-driven neural framework for discovering dynamically admissible extreme scenarios. Rather than assuming prior knowledge of the governing equations, the first stage infers the effective dynamical constraints directly from observational data. When the underlying physical system possesses suitable symmetries, the learned dynamics can be represented in a geometry-agnostic form, independent of any fixed grid, coordinate system, dimensionality, and intrinsic curvature. In the second stage, a physics-informed neural-search uses this learned dynamics to uncover rare, high-impact coherent structures that may not have appeared in the original observations. We demonstrate this framework through representative examples of increasing dimensionality and geometric complexity. Starting from a traditionally learned Duffing dynamics, we find a homoclinic pulse as a plausible localized extreme scenario. Next, since the same equation also appears in the stationary nonlinear Schrodinger system, with the coordinate interpreted as space instead of time, this pulse becomes a standing soliton. We then retrain the first stage using a geometry-agnostic neural representation, enabling the learned dynamics to be lifted to higher-dimensional space to obtain higher-dimensional solitary profile, known as Townes soliton. Finally, with a Liouville system, we demonstrate that dynamics learned from data on a (1+1)-dimensional Lorentzian quasi-manifold can be transferred to a (2+0)-dimensional Euclidean manifold to identify an instanton. Our approach can be applied to other coherent spatiotemporal structures, including kinks, rogue waves, compactons, peakons, and potentially even singularities, with applications in risk analysis, nonlinear forecasting, and anomaly detection.

title: Discrete Exterior Calculus-based Whittle-Matérn Fields on Meshes
abstract: This work presents a sparse precision formulation for Whittle-Matérn fields based on Discrete Exterior Calculus. By treating the $k$-cochain as the latent object to be modeled, we show that a single formulation can produce Whittle-Matérn fields for all $k$ and integer $α$ values. By utilising Whitney maps we can enable a push-forward of the prior on 1-cochains, enabling inference for discrete vector fields. We demonstrate this model on interpolation of vector fields on a sphere.

title: Asymmetric Looped Transformers: Fixed Global Representations for an Iterative Decoder
abstract: Looped Transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying shared layers, offering a way to scale computation without increasing parameter count. However, full-stack looping places context construction and iterative state refinement within the same recurrent computation, without explicitly distinguishing their roles. We introduce the Asymmetric Looped Transformer (AsymLoop), which separates single-pass context encoding from recurrent state refinement. A single-pass causal encoder produces layer-specific Global key-value (KV) caches that remain fixed across iterations, while a weight-tied recurrent decoder generates Local KV from its evolving state. Joint attention over both sources under a single softmax allows each update to integrate persistent contextual information with the current intermediate state. For training, we apply a heavy-tail-guided layerwise learning-rate method to the encoder and decoder. Experiments on FineWeb-Edu across four model scales, from 60M to 1B, show consistently lower validation perplexity and higher average downstream accuracy than Full Loop under matched effective depth and training token budgets. At 1B, AsymLoop improves average zero-shot accuracy across seven commonsense reasoning benchmarks from 49.58% to 50.85%. Further experiments extend these benefits to longer training budgets, an OLMo-style backbone, and sparse mixture-of-experts models. These results support asymmetric context encoding and state refinement as an effective design for recurrent language models.

title: Learning from Automatic 3D Gaussian Splatting Edits for Online Bayesian Scene Change Detection
abstract: Online scene change detection requires integrating incoming observations to determine which regions have changed relative to a reference scene. We update change beliefs as new images arrive using generalised Bayesian evidence fusion. However, the prior probability of change and evidence models are unknown beforehand, and numerical Bayesian inference can be costly. We address these challenges by learning offline from automatic edits to a reference 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) model. These edits generate labelled training views without manual annotations. Together with unchanged reference observations, they provide supervision for learning scene-specific evidence models and estimating the effective pixel prior and response statistics. Online prediction combines current evidence with historical support, while closed-form local Bayes factors, parameterized by the learned response statistics, update an accumulated 3D Gaussian field. Object-guided refinement produces the final change masks. Our method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on PASLCD and CCS3D, with $67.64\%$ and $75.82\%$ mIoU, respectively. On PASLCD, the complete pipeline runs at $17.2$\,FPS over complete query sequences, the fastest among the evaluated online methods.

title: OptionWorld: A Benchmark for Diagnosing Failures of LLMs as Long-Term Personal Assistants
abstract: Long-term assistants must follow unfinished tasks across days as information and circumstances change. Finding information or starting an action, however, does not ensure that the task gets completed. We introduce OptionWorld, a benchmark that traces information acquisition, judgments, actions, and outcomes in simulated daily-life tasks to identify where current LLMs fall short as long-term personal assistants. In runs with archived decision inputs, the key facts remain in the model's last input before the deadline in 35.5% of failed instances. Failure analysis identifies the three most frequent problems: needed information is not obtained or combined, available opportunities to act go unused, and agents impose restrictions that the task does not require. Three follow-up experiments show that supplying missing facts restores task success in some cases; action reminders can restart work while subsequent steps still miss the deadline; and correcting a supplied note that wrongly forbids contact restores permitted inquiry. These findings locate shortcomings in maintaining task state: connecting facts to unfinished work, following through before deadlines, and separating actual restrictions from the agent's assumptions.

title: Toda chain solves large BKP
abstract: We prove that any solution of the Toda chain hierarchy (the 1D reduction of the 2D Toda lattice) is a solution of the large BKP hierarchy. This is a difference analogue of Alexandrov's result that KdV solves (small) BKP.

title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
abstract: A first-principles-informed multiscale modeling approach is reported for oxide formation during corrosion of zirconium. The present simulations reproduce the columnar corrosion film microstructure and grain size distribution seen in micrographs of oxidized Zr surfaces. This structural feature emerges from a hexagonal ZrO layer adjacent to the $α$-Zr/ZrO$_{2-x}$ interface, which is dynamically stabilized by continuous heterogeneous grain nucleation and grain boundary mass diffusion. This ZrO layer is identified as a significant oxygen diffusion barrier and a potential contributor to sub-parabolic pretransition corrosion kinetics. The simulations also reproduce the undulatory nature of the metal/oxide interface, leading to regions with tensile stress components capable of nucleating cracks, despite the overall state of compressive hydrostatic stress within the oxide film. First principles density functional theory (DFT) computations of fundamental ZrO$_x$ properties were combined with molecular dynamics simulations using a machine-learned potential based on a DFT training set to provide extensive input to an advanced phase field model for oxide formation and its microstructure, as implemented in the new MedeA PhaseField module. The phase field simulations reported herein incorporated computed stoichiometry-dependent thermochemical data, anisotropic elastic properties, interface energies, bulk and grain boundary mass transport processes, multiphase heterogeneous grain nucleation, and strain energy-dependent phase stabilities.

title: Photonic band structure by direct second-kind free-space boundary integral equations
abstract: We present a direct boundary integral equation (BIE) formulation of the Bloch eigenvalue problem for two-dimensional photonic crystals that uses only the free-space Helmholtz Green function. The unknowns are the Cauchy data of the Bloch mode on the inclusion boundary and on two cell walls. On the inclusion boundary, the transmission conditions are imposed via Müller's formulation. The wall equations, in turn, come from a stack formulation, in which Green's formula is applied on stacks of three cells, so that the wall self-interactions and the interactions between arcs sharing endpoints cancel exactly. The resulting system is of the second kind, Fredholm of index zero, and free of corner singularities, and the walls may be curved to keep the cell boundary away from the inclusions. Its operators are assembled once per frequency and reused for all Bloch vectors. We prove that every Bloch mode yields a nonzero null vector, and that a null vector comes from a Bloch mode exactly when its cell representation vanishes outside the cell, which gives an inexpensive test for spurious null vectors. The band frequencies are computed with a high-order Nyström discretization and the search of Bruno, Santana and Trefethen, which locates them as poles of adaptive Antoulas--Anderson (AAA) rational approximants to a randomly scalarized resolvent sampled on the real frequency axis. Numerical examples validate the method against exact and published band structures and include a challenging triangular lattice of air pores in a dielectric, whose cell requires curved walls.

title: Model- and Layer-Level Closed-Loop Forecasting with SSM-Based Spiking Neural Networks
abstract: Deep State-Space Models (Deep SSMs) have shown promising performance and computational benefits in processing of time-series data with complex temporal dependencies. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) constitute a biologically inspired class of deep SSMs, where computing blocks communicate through spikes, discrete single-bit events rather than continuous activation functions. A particularly important task in time-series processing is forecasting, i.e. predicting future values of a sequence from past observations alone. However, how to best perform forecasting with SNNs is an open question, where the standard autoregressive nature of the data processing with SNNs requires values that are not available during the forecasting phase. In this article, we address this challenge. We explore two closed-loop forecasting strategies, in which the network's own generated values are fed back into the network as if they were observed past values: (i) model-level and (ii) layer-level closed-loop forecasting. We evaluate these approaches on the ETT-small datasets, a standard benchmark for time-series forecasting, under both spike-based and continuous activation functions. We compare the proposed closed-loop approaches against state-of-the-art methods such as SpaceTime, as well as the zero-masking baseline in S4. Both of the proposed approaches perform comparably to or better than zero-masking with S4, and in most cases match SpaceTime. These findings highlight the trade-off between continuous and low-bit quantized activations, and demonstrate that the proposed Deep SSM architectures provide a competitive framework for forecasting.

title: Delayed Convergence of S-Parameter Sensitivities to Design Parameters in FDTD Simulations
abstract: In the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, the sensitivities of S-parameters to design parameters come from discrete Fourier transforms of responses ending at a simulation time T. We show that, when a design parameter moves a resonance, the sensitivity converges later than the S-parameter. For a single mode with field decay time $τ$, the truncation error of the sensitivity is $(1+T/τ)e^{-T/τ}$, against $e^{-T/τ}$ for the resonant part of the S-parameter, so a 1% sensitivity error needs $T \geq 6.6τ$ instead of $4.6τ$. Automatic differentiation, the discrete adjoint and finite differences on the same run carry this error, so their agreement cannot reveal it. In three solvers, with no fitted parameter, the estimate predicts the simulated error within 4% at cavity resonances with $Q$ of 1000-7000; at lower $Q$ the error is larger. On a cavity whose slowest mode is weakly coupled, common end criteria leave $|S_{11}|$ within 0.5 dB of a 1.3 dB dip but its sensitivity 10-72% in error. A matrix-pencil extrapolation inside the differentiable computation recovers the sensitivity on a cavity with field probes from a run 66 times shorter. In a single-pole filter loop with a symmetric objective, truncation leaves the maximum of the objective in place, and the optimizer reaches the resonance of a full run despite the wrong gradient. With two coupled poles, the truncated objective moves the optimum: on runs of $1τ$ it over-couples by $Δk \approx 1.24/Q$, and an equal-ripple objective still shifts it by about $0.2\barα$ at $3τ$, but not at $4.6τ$.

title: Matrix divisors, Christoffel transformations and symmetric $d$-connections
abstract: The Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ relates elementary bundle modifications to gap probability recurrences. The moment matrix determines normalization and the splitting type. We define the source and target moduli problems by their local data. The modifications identify common stable loci and conjugate their point-addition maps. For Pearson ratios $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $°d=1,2$, we construct rational spectral coordinates and compute the induced transformation. For positive even weights with finite moments, reweighting configurations yields the transformed gap probability recurrence. Its coefficient is a rational function of the transformed spectral coordinates. A local formula applies outside these charts under the stated hypotheses.

title: Present but Hard to Read: Probing Latent Reasoning with Minimal Pairs
abstract: Probing studies of latent reasoning often read a model's state where the answer begins and take a failed probe as evidence that a value is absent. We test this with a digit copied from the question, in the looped model Ouro-1.4B and the standard transformer Qwen2.5-1.5B. Comparing prompts that differ only in that digit shows it is present at the last prompt token, in a code shared across questions (readout about 0.9). A probe that sees one prompt at a time, the usual setting, barely reads it: 0.36 in Ouro and 0.19 in Qwen even after 5,249 training questions. The digit's change is small rather than crowded: random noise lands on equally busy directions, while a random word in its place moves the state far more and is readable. Since every varied token leaves a trace, a successful probe is ambiguous too. We give a protocol, including a synthetic null for generic mixing, for testing computed values against copies and mixtures of the inputs. In pre-registered studies of two-step problems it finds a small signal for the unwritten intermediate a+b just before Ouro writes the answer's last digit, and its sign follows the operation, though mixing alone produces much of that sign-following part. Holding that value at another problem's from the first loop on does not move the written digit toward the other problem's, while the same patch of the answer does: the value is readable but not used.

title: Quadratic hulls of osculating varieties of rational normal curves
abstract: Let $T^p c_r$ be the $p$-osculating variety of the rational normal curve $c_r\subset\mathbb{P}S^r(\mathbb{C}^2)$. We study its quadratic hull, the scheme defined by the quadratic equations vanishing on $T^p c_r$. For $r\ge2p+3$, we prove that this scheme is a complete intersection of $\binom{r-2p}{2}$ quadrics whenever \[ p\ge\binom{r-2p-1}{2}. \] When the inequality is strict, the hull is integral and strictly contains $T^p c_r$. On the boundary its support is reducible, except for $(p,r)=(1,5)$, where the hull equals the osculating variety. The proof is local at the highest weight point. Koornwinder's relation between Clebsch--Gordan coefficients and Hahn polynomials leads to a description of the tangent-cone equations in which each antidiagonal becomes an ordinary polynomial space of bounded degree. An incidence estimate then gives a normal integral tangent cone in the strict range, and the $SL_2$-action turns this local statement into global integrality.

title: BitMTP: When Multi-Token Prediction Meets Low-Bit Large Language Models
abstract: For efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs), methods of ultra-low-bit backbones reduce weight storage, memory traffic, and linear-layer execution cost, while multi-token prediction (MTP) methods reduce sequential decoding steps by predicting multiple future tokens in parallel. Although complementary, the direct combination of these methods cannot accelerate decoding at comparable quality: masked drafting lacks intermediate token input supplied in next-token training, while wider computation and causal key-value (KV) updates can offset the savings from fewer steps. To address these challenges, we propose BitMTP, an algorithm-system co-design framework for efficient MTP on ultra-low-bit LLM backbones. A joint next-token prediction and MTP objective equips a single model with both autoregressive (AR) generation and block-causal drafting. Confidence-only decoding, speculative-only decoding, and hybrid decoding provide different quality-throughput operating points without using separate draft and verifier models. Accepted-prefix alignment keeps the committed prefix, materialized causal KV boundary, and CUDA Graph replay state consistent for continued generation. BitMTP uses this contract to select width-specialized low-bit execution and reuse captured graphs over shared KV storage. On NVIDIA H20, BitMTP with hybrid decoding achieves five-task mean speedups of 2.2x on BitNet b1.58-2B and 2.1-2.4x on 1.7B-4B Bonsai models at comparable task quality. On RTX 3090 and Jetson Orin, it further achieves up to 2.0x in five-task mean throughput and 3.3x on MBPP+, respectively. These results demonstrate that BitMTP accelerates ultra-low-bit LLM generation across backbones, model sizes, and GPU types. The source code is released at https://github.com/PolyU-VCLab/BitMTP

title: Improved Approximation for Unsplittable Capacitated Vehicle Routing Using Quota Trees
abstract: In the Unsplittable Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (UCVRP), we are given a set $V$ of $n$ clients with normalized demands $d_v \in (0,1]$, a depot $r$, a unit vehicle capacity, and symmetric metric travel costs $c$ on $V \cup \{r\}$. We seek a collection of routes of minimum total cost that start and end at $r$, serve each client's entire demand on a single route, and respect the unit capacity constraint $\sum_{v \in V(R)} d_v \le 1$ on every route $R$, where $V(R)$ denotes the clients served by $R$. This models deliveries from a common depot in which each customer's order must be delivered in a single trip. UCVRP generalizes the metric traveling salesman problem (TSP) and is therefore NP-hard. Capacity constraints add a packing difficulty: when all clients are colocated away from the depot, minimizing the route cost is equivalent to minimizing the number of bins in bin packing. Consequently, UCVRP admits no polynomial-time approximation ratio below $3/2$ unless $\textbf{P=NP}$ (Grandoni, Mathieu, and Zhou, 2023). The classical $3.5$-approximation has been improved through several recent advances; in particular, Zhao and Xiao (2026) recently obtained a $(2+\ln 2+\varepsilon)$-approximation. In this paper, we give a deterministic $(5/2+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm running in $n^{O(1/\varepsilon)}$ time for every rational $0<\varepsilon\le1/9$, applicable to general capacity and arbitrary positive demands. Our algorithm uses local search to select routes through one client with large demand and clients with small demands. It constructs candidate routes using endpoint quota trees after rounding demands and creating vertex copies. We combine these routes with those obtained by matching and set packing, keeping their client sets disjoint. The remaining clients are served by partitioning a tour constructed using weighted graphic matroid parity.

title: GazeLens for Efficient Egocentric Video Question Answering with Simple Gaze-Driven Adaptive Token Reduction
abstract: Smart glasses can help users understand their activities and surroundings, but small vision-language models must preserve useful evidence within limited computation. This is difficult because redundant frames consume the visual budget, while aggressive spatial compression can discard relevant details. Although gaze identifies the wearer's focus, the question may require evidence from the surrounding scene. To address these constraints, we propose GazeLens, which combines frame selection with gaze- and question-guided token reduction. First, HOG transitions and image sharpness select frames before visual encoding. For each selected frame, Gaussian pooling then forms gaze-focused and complementary summaries. Because their relevance depends on the question, a lightweight gate blends them into a primary token. Together with a global scene token, this retains both focused and contextual summaries within two tokens per frame. On StreamGaze, GazeLens achieves higher macro and micro accuracy than the evaluated full-grid and token-reduction baselines, with lower input-forward FLOPs than the shared-backbone token-reduction baselines.

title: Extremals for Sharp Trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev Inequalities on Convex Cones
abstract: Zugmeyer~\cite{Zug} established sharp trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequalities on convex cones for $a\geq n>p>1$. We classify all nonzero real-valued extremals of these inequalities. Let the cone be the epigraph of a finite convex function that is positively homogeneous of degree one, and let $H$ be any norm. We prove that equality holds precisely for functions of the form $A H(x+te+\ell)^{-(a-p)/(p-1)}$, where $A\in\mathbb{R}\backslash\{0\}$, $t>0$, $e=(0,\ldots,0,1)$, and $\ell$ belongs to the largest vector subspace contained in the cone. The result includes the critical Sobolev trace inequality at $a=n$, as well as nonsmooth norms and cones, half-spaces, and cones containing lines.

title: An exact formula for optimal axis-parallel packing of eight squares
abstract: We determine the smallest square container for eight axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths. The optimal side length is the minimum of the costs of 23 explicit packing strategies, and each cost is a maximum of sums of side lengths. No minimum of fewer convex functions represents it. Three strategies suffice for seven squares; the jump to 23 for eight squares witnesses the beginning of a combinatorial explosion. We prove the formula by combining the constructions with geometric lower bounds derived from disjoint coordinate projections, cornering arguments, and a weighted area comparison.

title: Blueprint for an AI-Enabled Particle Theory Community
abstract: Rapid advances in the capabilities and reach of artificial intelligence (AI) are changing research in particle physics. In this new era, AI is an innovative tool for theoretical physicists, while the interaction of AI and particle theory is itself a developing field. We argue that particle theory requires a community-scale effort to realize its full potential. We show how particle theory occupies a unique position in the AI for physics landscape, and describe the complementarity of AI and theory developments. We conclude with a series of recommendations on how to build an AI-enabled theory community for the Genesis Mission.

title: Isospin breaking in $ρππ$ couplings: $ρ^{+,0}$ width difference and muon $g-2$
abstract: The dominant contribution to the hadronic vaccum polarization (HVP) of the muon $g-2$ can be calculated using the hadronic spectrum in $τ^- \to π^-π^0ν_τ$ decay, provided isospin breaking (IB) corrections are properly accounted for. Among these corrections, IB in the $ρππ$ coupling has been pointed out as a missing ingredient. In this work, we calculate this IB effect within the impulse approximation using a symmetry-preserving framework based on Dyson-Schwinger and Bethe-Salpeter equations, incorporating fully dressed quark propagators and meson Bethe-Salpeter amplitudes. We then estimate its effect in the HVP contribution to the muon $g-2$. As a natural extension, we also compute the IB in the ratio of $ϕK^+K^-/ϕK^0\bar{K^0}$ couplings and compare with existing data. We obtain a coupling ratio $g_{ρ^0π^+π^-}/g_{ρ^+π^+π^0} = 1.0024(17)(1)$, which yields an isospin-breaking correction of $Δa_μ^{\mathrm{HVP,LO}}[ρππ] = -2.32(1.64)\times 10^{-10}$ to the two-pion contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment extracted from $τ$ decay data.

title: ECG for laboratory values:A comprehensive physiological and technical analysis
abstract: Laboratory measurements are essential for clinical decision making but typically require invasive blood sampling. Recent research suggests that ECG recordings may contain information beyond cardiac rhythm and provide information related to laboratory values. This thesis investigates NT-proBNP prediction from ECG recordings and patient metadata using a multimodal deep learning framework, while considering the physiological plausibility of ECG-based prediction. It also compares a 1-lead configuration using lead II with the corresponding 12-lead configuration. Additional experiments on glucose, hemoglobin, and potassium are presented in the appendix. Regression, binary classification, and three-class classification experiments were conducted using MIMIC-IV, with the three-class task based on clinically established thresholds. The 12-lead configuration consistently achieved better performance. Regression reached a mean absolute error of 534.98 pg/mL for 1-lead and 514.27 pg/mL for 12-lead. Binary classification achieved AUROCs of 0.849 and 0.876, respectively, while three-class classification achieved macro-averaged AUROCs of 0.738 and 0.752. The results indicate that precise NT-proBNP regression remains challenging, whereas broader concentration ranges can be classified more effectively. The findings are consistent with the physiological hypothesis that ECG characteristics and NT-proBNP concentrations reflect shared cardiovascular processes. ECG-based NT-proBNP prediction may therefore provide complementary information, particularly for classifying broader concentration ranges. However, laboratory measurements remain necessary, and validation on independent datasets is required.

title: Deep Learning-Based Road Lane Quality Assessment from Egocentric Dashcam Video
abstract: Reliable lane markings are important for both human drivers and automated driving systems, but their condition is still commonly assessed through manual inspection. Existing autonomous-driving datasets primarily support lane detection and scene understanding and usually lack maintenance-oriented labels for lane-marking visibility, continuity, or degradation. In this study, we present a geo-referenced smartphone dashcam dataset and baseline framework for lane-marking quality assessment. The dataset contains 63,839 road-facing frames collected across South Texas using a GPS-enabled dashcam application. A subset of 3,339 frames is matched with OpenStreetMap-derived lane-count labels, which are used as weak supervision for lane-count regression and map-consistency evaluation. We propose three lane-quality measures: Contrast Stability Index (CSI), which captures lane-background contrast using Laplacian responses; Line Continuity Ratio (LCR), which estimates structural continuity using edge and Hough-line evidence; and Regression Lane Confidence Score (RLCS), which measures agreement between predicted and map-derived lane counts on matched frames. The baseline prediction models attained strong performance, with CSI (MAE $0.039$, $R^2=0.97$) and LCR (MAE $0.093$, $R^2=0.84$). Notably, CSI and LCR are no-reference, segmentation-derived quality metrics that can be computed without dense human labels. In a pilot validation using 50 human-ranked images, these proposed lane-specific metrics show stronger rank agreement with human lane-quality ordering (e.g., Spearman's $ρ=0.7316$ and Kendall's $τ=0.5472$ for LCR) than general image-quality measures such as PSNR, SSIM, BRISQUE, NIQE, and LPIPS. We believe the dataset, metrics, and baseline provide an initial step toward scalable, low-cost, location-aware lane-marking quality assessment. Data and code: https://github.com/Shaif95/Road_Quality

title: Shell-model description of collective deformation variables $β$ and $γ$ in $^{164-188}$Hf nuclei
abstract: Symmetry-based models, such as the pseudo-SU(3) scheme, have proved to be highly useful tools for describing the low-energy structure of nuclei in the rare-earth region. This model is employed to study the evolution of the collective deformation variables beta and gamma in the ground state (0+) along the isotopic chain 164-188Hf.
